content: Microdroplets have become widely used in various fields due to their advantages of high heat and mass transfer efficiency [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723030346#b0005), high controllability [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723030346#b0010), and high sensitivity [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723030346#b0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723030346#b0020). However, traditional [emulsification](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/emulsification "Learn more about emulsification from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") methods struggle with low production efficiency and poor monodispersion of products, making it difficult to meet high requirements for droplet uniformity in certain fields, such as biological research [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723030346#b0025), drug delivery [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723030346#b0030), and high-end chemical production. Microchemical [technology](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/science-and-technology "Learn more about technology from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") based on microchannel provides a novel platform for the precise control of microdroplets, where most methods use the shearing force applied by an immiscible cross-flowing fluid at a T-junction or cross-junction to generate droplets.

In recent years, [microfluidic technology](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidic- technology "Learn more about microfluidic technology from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") has played an important role in [engineering applications](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/engineering- application "Learn more about engineering applications from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), such as [inkjet printing](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/inkjet-printing "Learn more about inkjet printing from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") ([Basaran et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0003); [Li et al., 2015](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0021)), Micro-array chip ([Labanieh et al., 2015](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0019)) and medicine ([Boskovic and Loebbecke, 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0004)), but there are still difficulties in realizing the numbering-up of [microchannels](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microchannel "Learn more about microchannels from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"). It is found that the introducing of the crossing flow into the microchannel system can enhance the transport performance of the continuous phase and the multi-phase mixing effect ([Capretto et al., 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0007) and [Waqas et al., 2022](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0031)). Therefore, it is necessary to investigate the dynamic of droplets in the crossing flow in multi-branched microchannels, in which the retraction and break-up of liquid filaments is very important. However, it is not yet possible to obtain whether the liquid filaments collapse stably into a single droplet or irregularly into a series of satellite droplets. Significant progress has been made in the dynamics of liquid filaments, such as extensional rheology of complex fluids, deformation of liquid bridges, and capillary rupture of filaments etc ([McKinley and Sridhar, 2002](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0024); [Sujatha et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0028); [Yildirim and Basaran, 2001](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0033)). It was also found that the stability of liquid filaments is related to the viscosity of fluids, aspect ratio and initial disturbance. The stability of filaments strongly affects the number and size distribution of satellite droplets. Furthermore, studies have shown that the viscous filaments _Oh_ ≫1 are always stable ( _Oh_ is a [dimensionless number](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/dimensionless-number "Learn more about dimensionless number from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") that measures the interaction of [viscous force](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/viscous-force "Learn more about viscous force from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") with [inertial force](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/inertial- force "Learn more about inertial force from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") and surface tension, _Oh_ = _μ_ ( _ρLγ_ )−0.5, _μ_ is the [dynamic viscosity](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/dynamic-viscosity "Learn more about dynamic viscosity from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") of the liquid, _ρ_ is the density of the liquid, _γ_ is the surface tension, _L_ is the characteristic length scale (typically drop diameter)), and the rupture of the viscous filament is mainly due to the Rayleigh-Plateau instability ([Driessen et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0013)). [Wang et al. (2019)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0030) established a capillary wave superposition model and confirmed that the breakup was caused by the [mutual interference](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/mutual- interference "Learn more about mutual interference from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") of the capillary waves generated at the end of the liquid filament. Plateau et al. ([Plateau et al., 1873](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0034)) found that if the perturbation wavelength is larger than the circumference of the jet, the varicose vein perturbation of the liquid jet is inevitable. [Brasz et al. (2018)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0005) numerically simulated the retraction of an approximately inviscid conical filament by introducing self-similar perturbations into the system, and found that the perturbation amplitude must exceed a threshold to form satellite droplets. [Anthony et al. (2019)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0001) considered the entire possible range of fluid properties and initial aspect ratios of filaments, providing a complete phase diagram of the filament retraction kinetics. [Kamat et al. (2020)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0017) analyzed the vorticity dynamics and vorticity balance of recoil filaments, illustrating how [surface tension gradients](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/surface-tension- gradient "Learn more about surface tension gradients from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") and [Marangoni](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/marangoni "Learn more about Marangoni from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") stress cause recoil filaments to escape from end-pinching. Considering that the filament rupture is essentially the destabilizing process of the limited liquid jet, its stability is closely related to the liquid jet. In applications such as [atomization](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/atomisation "Learn more about atomization from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), spraying, and inkjet printing, satellite droplets formed by the shrinkage of liquid filaments often lead to volume deviations of the target product ([Basaran, 2002](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222002518#bib0002)). Therefore, it is imperative to fully understand the formation mechanism of satellite droplets and then to suppress satellite droplets.

Making micro-sized droplets in a controlled size and flow pattern has been recently one of the attractive research areas related to [microfluidics](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidics "Learn more about microfluidics from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") in various applications such as consumer products of mono-dispersed micro particles, food processing, pharmaceuticals for drug delivery, cosmetics, tumor annihilation, synthesis of nanoparticles, enhancement of mixing reactions for chemical industries, creation of emulsions, crystallization of proteins, personal [health care products](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/healthcare-product "Learn more about health care products from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") and bubble generators among others [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b1), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b2), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b3). Numerous research groups have experimentally investigated several features of droplet formation. There are a variety of devices that can be used to generate droplets in [micro scale](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microscale "Learn more about micro scale from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"). There exist three major methods for droplet generation in [microfluidic devices](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidic-device "Learn more about microfluidic devices from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"): hydrodynamic flow focusing in co-flowing fluids [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b4), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b5), T-junctions [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b6), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b7), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b8), [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b9), [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b10), [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b11), [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b12), [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b13), and immiscible fluids mixing by the orifice [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b14), [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b15), [[16]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b16), [[17]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b17), [[18]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b18), [[19]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S209503491730079X#b19). Among these methods in microfluidic devices, cross-flow shear in micro channels with T-junctions and flow-focusing configurations strongly depend upon the geometrical parameters controlling the break-up of droplets.

Droplet-based [microfluidics](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/microfluidics "Learn more about microfluidics from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") is an active research field that presents great potential for high- throughput chemical and biological analysis, synthesis of advanced materials, sample [pretreatment](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/pretreatment "Learn more about pretreatment from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), [protein crystallization](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/protein- crystallization "Learn more about protein crystallization from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") and encapsulation of cells [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400514001907#bib0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400514001907#bib0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400514001907#bib0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400514001907#bib0020). In these devices, droplets of a fluid forming the so-called [dispersed phase](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/dispersed-phase "Learn more about dispersed phase from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") are carried by the stream of a second immiscible fluid identified as the continuous phase. Depending on the application, two major types of droplets are usually produced: water-in-oil (W/O) or oil-in-water (O/W) droplets.

Two-phase [microfluidic](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidics "Learn more about microfluidic from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") flows are involved in variety of applications including lab-on-a-chip devices ([Baroud et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0142727X18304685#bib0005)), food and pharmaceutical industries, [inkjet printing](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/inkjet-printing "Learn more about inkjet printing from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") ([Baroud and Willaime, 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0142727X18304685#bib0006)), electronic cooling ([Lewis et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0142727X18304685#bib0028), [Revellin and Thome, 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0142727X18304685#bib0036)), etc. Two-phase [microfluidic devices](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidic-device "Learn more about microfluidic devices from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") usually have two separate microchannels/tubes through which different phases enter the system. The geometry of the junction where these channels intersect strongly influences the flow condition. Numerous microfluidic device configurations have been designed and tested, but the most popular geometries which have been used for drop formation and heat removal are coaxial, flow- focusing and T-junction configurations ([Nunes et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0142727X18304685#bib0031)).

Micro-fluidic chips have emerged as a novel tool for conducting chemical and biomedical processes in a miniaturized platform for the past two decades. Reagents can significantly decrease to micro-liters or nano-liters, and the reaction time could be shortened to a few seconds or less. One micro-fluidic subaggregate is a form of micro-droplet technology that can precisely manipulate mono-disperse micro-droplets, including their generation, fission, fusion, inside mixing, [double emulsion](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/multiple-emulsion "Learn more about double emulsion from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), sorting, and surface treatment. Micro-droplets have wide applications in micro-chemical reactors, targeting drug delivery, [biochemical](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/biochemicals "Learn more about biochemical from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") reactions, cell cultivation and encapsulation, and [protein crystallization](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/protein- crystallization "Learn more about protein crystallization from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"). Song et al. [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1359431115001659#bib1) recently reviewed biological and chemical reactions in droplets in micro- fluidic channels and reported the advantages and challenges in manipulating droplets as reactors and synthesis of micro-particles.

Recently, a new class of two-dimensional (2D) materials, such as [transition metal carbides](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/transition-metal-carbide "Learn more about transition metal carbides from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), [nitrides](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/nitride "Learn more about nitrides from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") and carbon nitrides (MXenes), have attracted worldwide attention due to their rich chemical and physical properties [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0015). The chemical formula of MXenes is Mn+1XnTx (n = 1, 2, or 3), where M represents transition metal (e.g., Sc, Ti, Zr, Hf, Nb, Ta, Cr, Mo, Mn), X denotes C and/or N, Tx is surface functional group (e.g., hydroxyl, oxygen or fluorine) [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0025), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0030), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0035). So far, over 30 different kinds of MXenes have been experimentally obtained and many more MXenes are theoretically predicted to exist [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0040), [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0045), [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0050), [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0055). MXenes have been found to demonstrate tailorable and excellent properties due to their abundant surface functional groups and stoichiometry. Especially, MXenes have been proved to have high optical transmittance in visible light region. Ti3C2Tx, in particular, has shown a transmittance of ~93% with a [conductivity](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/conductivity "Learn more about conductivity from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") of ~5736 S cm−1 when its thickness is down to ~4 nm [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0060), [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0065). Also, the large tunability of work functions from ~2.14 eV to ~5.65 eV could be readily to achieve, covering a wide range of metals [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0070). Benefiting from these appealing properties, outstanding [photodetection](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/photodetection "Learn more about photodetection from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") performance has been demonstrated based on MXenes in previous studies [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0075), [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0070). Meanwhile, optical and electronic properties of MXenes are considered to be tailored by the surface terminations, transition metals, electrochemical intercalation, thickness and so on [[16]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0080). Consequently, these excellent [optoelectronic](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/optoelectronics "Learn more about optoelectronic from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") properties, combined with hydrophilia, high transmittance, and high [electrical conductivity](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/electrical-conductivity "Learn more about electrical conductivity from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") make MXenes attractive and promising candidates for the important applications in optoelectronic devices and systems, such as [energy storage and conversion](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/energy-storage- and-conversion "Learn more about energy storage and conversion from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") devices [[17]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0085), [electromagnetic interference](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/electromagnetic- [[18]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0264127521004032#b0090), [transparent conductors](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/transparent-conducting-film "Learn Yield stress non-Newtonian fluid (YSF) - a typical complex fluid is widely used in food, cosmetics, pharmaceutical industries etc. ([Laborie et al., 2016](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092300252X#b0110), [Laborie et al., 2016](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092300252X#b0105), [Laborie et al., 2015](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092300252X#b0100)). Below the critical yield stress ( _τ_ c), YSF appears at solid state, otherwise liquid state. The relationship between viscosity and shear rate can be expressed by Herschel-Bulkley (H-B) constitutive equation:(1)τ<τc⇒γ̇=0(solid regime)τ<τc⇒τ=τc+kγ̇n(liquid regime)where _τ c_ is the critical yield stress, Pa; _k_ is the consistency coefficient, indicating the viscous characteristics, Pa·s _n_ ; _n_ is the rheological index of fluid, indicating non-Newtonian characteristics.

Droplet fluidic systems have dramatically improved precision in many applications, such as polymerase chain reaction ([Tanaka et al., 2015](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0130)), biochemical analysis ([Kim et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0070)), and particle synthesis ([DeMello, 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0030)) in which accurate control of sample volume play a significant role. Despite the well-understood physics of squeezing regime droplet formation in two-phase flow systems, the long-sought-after goal of generating identical, equal size droplets is challenging. Although the individual parameters that affect the droplet size were identified as channel dimension ([Thorsen et al., 2001](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0135)), wettability ([Xu et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0165)), viscosity ([Nekouei and Vanapalli, 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0105)), and flow rate or pressure ratio of the two immiscible fluids ([Garstecki et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0040), [Ward et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0155), [Xu et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0160)), the governing mechanism of droplet size variation is not completely analysed. It is shown that droplet length is correlated to the pressure ([Ward et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0155)) or flow rate ([Garstecki et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0040), [Van Steijn et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0140), [Xu et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0160)) ratio of the dispersed and continuous phases. There are studies that discuss the root causes of size variation as internal and external pressure fluctuation ([Glawdel and Ren, 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0045), [Korczyk et al., 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0075), [van Steijn et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0145)). While the consequences of such fluctuations are still incompletely understood, some methods have been proposed to decrease internal ([Pang et al., 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0115)) and external fluctuations ([Crawford et al., 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0020), [Kalantarifard et al., 2018](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0060), [Kang and Yang, 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0065)). These approaches suffer from experimental complexity and do not lead to a comprehensive solution for the elimination of pressure and flow rate fluctuations. Here, we introduce a new approach to analyse droplet size variation that eventually leads to a thorough understanding of the root causes of droplet polydispersity. We demonstrate ultra-monodisperse droplet generation with a coefficient of variation (CV) close to the theoretical limit of 0% CV. We extend the basic electric circuits analogy of fluidic circuits ([Mosadegh et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0095), [Oh et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920306254#b0110)) to develop a methodology to study the key parameters that affect droplet size variation. Applying high identical pressure from a single pressure supply and using a low hydrodynamic resistance droplet channel are the key factors for monodisperse droplet generation.

[Microfluidics](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/microfluidics "Learn more about Microfluidics from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") is the branch of science and technology devoted to manipulate small amounts of fluids (from 10−9 to 10−10 L) in channels with characteristic dimensions of ten to hundreds of micrometers [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2214785320371339#b0005). Microfluidic platforms like lab-on-a-chip (LOC) or [micro total analysis systems](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials-science/micro-total- analysis-system "Learn more about micro total analysis systems from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") (µTAS) have become very popular because of its objective of narrowing the gap between classical laboratories or pilot factories to the microscale volume common in biology [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2214785320371339#b0010). Working at a microscale level gives microfluidics several advantages over its macro-scale counterparts. As the fluid dimension shrinks to the microscale, the surface-to-volume ratio increases and, therefore, the fluid behavior changes. Three main phenomena can be characterized [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2214785320371339#b0015); the improvement of mass and heat transfer; the dominance of viscous forces over inertial forces, which is reflected in the laminar regime; and surface effects, such as interfacial tension or capillary forces, become more significant.

A look at the current state of chemical, biochemical and life science research shows methods and protocols more or less the same for decades. These protocols are mostly cumbersome: a laboratory scientist spends hours mixing solutions in beakers, dispensing fluids drop by drop into microtiter plates, waiting for reactions to take place, and analyzing results by inspection or with the aid of expensive equipment. The microfluidics has emerged primarily for improving these time-intensive methods [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077907003803#bib1). The scaling-down of conventional macroscale processes takes advantages of high surface-volume ratio and enables smaller volumes, less waste, higher throughput, higher efficiency and accuracy, and the potential for process automation. Indeed, many scientists and researchers believe that microfluidics will be the key technology of revolutionizing the fields of analytical chemistry, biochemistry, biology and medicine by transforming them from the largely empirical sciences that they are presently into more mature and precise sciences.

Nanoliter-sized droplets are increasingly used as nano-reactors in chemistry, for crystallization ([Li et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915005321#bib1), [Selimovic et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915005321#bib2)), reaction ([Li and Ismagilov, 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915005321#bib3)) and analysis ([Zare and Kim, 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915005321#bib4), [Brouzes et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915005321#bib5), [Burns et al., 1998](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915005321#bib6)) studies. First, less material is consumed in nanoliter-sized droplets than in milliliter crystallizers. It is important to reduce material consumption when only small quantities of material are available, i.e. rare molecules such as pharmaceutical ingredients, purified proteins, or dangerous materials (energetic materials). Second, generating hundreds of nanoliter-sized droplets permits statistical analysis. Therefore microfluidic technologies are used with two-phase non-miscible flows, through flow-focusing ([Gañán-Calvo and Gordillo, 2001](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915005321#bib7), [Anna et al., 2003](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915005321#bib8)), co-flowing ([Umbanhowar et al., 1999](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915005321#bib9), [Garstecki et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915005321#bib10)) and cross-flowing ([Thorsen et al., 2001](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915005321#bib11), [Garstecki et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915005321#bib12)). In our application, the microfluidic system is dedicated to droplet-based crystallization experiments. Nanoliter volumes makes it possible to nucleate a limited number of crystals that we can locate easily, and the generation of hundreds of nanoliter-sized droplets allows stochasticity of nucleation to be addressed [Candoni et al. (2012)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915005321#bib13). Therefore, our purpose is to generate hundreds of droplets identical in size and composition. Moreover, as we mix different solutions before the generation of droplets, the droplets׳ spatial homogeneity is also a crucial consideration.

Bubble-based gas–liquid mixing processes are paramount in [chemical engineering](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/chemical-engineering "Learn more about chemical engineering from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), biology, materials science, drug manufacturing, and environmental treatment [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723014894#b0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723014894#b0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723014894#b0015), with gas–liquid [photochemistry](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth- and-planetary-sciences/photochemical-reaction "Learn more about photochemistry from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") as a prominent example [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723014894#b0020). In recent years, the rapid developments in photocatalysis have led to advancements in photocatalytic conversions involving gases, including [carbon dioxide capture](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/carbon-dioxide-capture "Learn more about carbon dioxide capture from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723014894#b0025), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723014894#b0030), hydrogenation [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723014894#b0035), [oxidation](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/oxidation-reaction "Learn more about oxidation from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723014894#b0040), and organic synthesis [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723014894#b0045). In numerous cases, the obstructed [gas diffusion](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/gaseous-diffusion "Learn more about gas diffusion from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") into the liquid phase and limited light-penetration depth decrease the efficiency of such processes [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723014894#b0050), [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723014894#b0055). Conventional gas–liquid systems often utilize gas bubbling in batch reactors or pressurized reaction vessels to improve the interphase mass transfer [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723014894#b0060), [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723014894#b0065). However, these methods suffer from insufficient interfacial contact, poor process controllability, and considerable safety risks [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723014894#b0070). Furthermore, these techniques are not applicable to photocatalytic processes as the photoreactor requires specific materials and fabrication to ensure sufficient light penetration in accordance with the Lambert–Beer law [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894723014894#b0075). These issues become more prominent when these standard gas–liquid dispersion [technologies](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/science-and-technology "Learn more about technologies from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") are combined with photocatalysis, particularly for large-scale industrial applications.

Multiphase flow in microchannels has gained much interest in recent years given the numerous emerging applications of microfluidics that promise to provide technological innovations not realizable with conventional channels. Gas–liquid two-phase flows in microchannels often exhibit different flow behavior than macro-sized conduits, which allows for the precise control of the trajectory of fluidic particles. Significant developments in the area of micro-scale fabrication have allowed researchers to construct increasingly more intricate devices.

Microfluidics allows precise control over chemical and biological investigations at micron scales that are comparable to the dimensions of the biological cell. As a result, microfluidic detection and analysis of single cells has seen a tremendous rise [[30](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0150),[35](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0175),[48](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0240)] and has enabled lab-on-chip and point-of-care applications [[9](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0045),[22](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0110),[31](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0155),[42](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0210),[47](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0235)]. In many microfluidic applications, cell detection is achieved using optical methods. Sensitive methods like fluorescence can allow molecule-specific detection enabling [cell classification](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/cell- classification "Learn more about cell classification from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages"). However, these methods require additional and sometimes tedious labelling steps [[45](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0225)]. Therefore, there have been parallel efforts to develop label-free assays for the detection and characterization of cells [[4](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0020),[25](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0125),[27](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0135),[32](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0160),[41](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0205),[55](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0275)]. One such promising technique for single cell analysis is Microfluidic Impedance Cytometry (MIC) which relies on cellular [electrical impedance](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials-science/electrical- impedance "Learn more about electrical impedance from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") [[18](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0090),[20](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0100)]. The [dielectric properties](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/dielectric-property "Learn more about dielectric properties from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") of a biological cell are defined by cellular characteristics like cell volume, composition and architecture. Continuous flow microfluidic devices with embedded microelectrodes for electrical measurements can be employed for detecting and classifying single cells in a high [throughput manner](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/throughput-manner "Learn more about throughput manner from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [[8](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0040),[17](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0085),[19](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0095),[20](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0100),[46](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0230),[50](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0250),[54](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0270)]. In most MIC devices, as the cell suspended in an electrolyte flows over an array of metal electrode pairs connected to a high frequency AC [excitation source](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/excitation-source "Learn more about excitation source from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), the dielectric properties of the media between the electrodes change. This in turn attenuates the measured impedance at a particular frequency across the microelectrode pair and generates a peak in the [differential output](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/differential-output "Learn more about differential output from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"). Highly sensitive MIC based detection has already shown promise in characterization of sub-cellular features and to monitor biomolecular reactions [[20](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0100),[29](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0145),[50](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167931719301613#bb0250)].

Nanoparticles have made a remarkable impact in biomedical applications as drug delivery carriers, non-viral vectors for gene therapy, labelling and tracking agents for imaging and diagnosis etc. [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0928493114006067#bb0005). They are characterised by having a higher cellular uptake compared to [microparticles](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/microparticle "Learn more about microparticles from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), which can be beneficial in decreasing the required dosage of the administrated drug [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0928493114006067#bb0010). Nanoparticles also have a better chance to fulfil their therapeutic purpose as they undergo a lower intensity of opsonisation reactions caused by the accumulation of proteins on the surface of the particles, thus they are able to avoid the fast immune response leading to clearance from the body [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0928493114006067#bb0015). Nanoparticles with sizes between 70 and 200 nm are found to have the longest circulation time in the body in comparison with larger particles [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0928493114006067#bb0020). A longer circulation time for a drug carrier in the blood flow can cause better absorbance and sustained release for the administrated drug, which is an important contributor for the efficiency and success of a drug carrier [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0928493114006067#bb0025). Therefore, nanoparticles are able to improve the treatment of a wide range of diseases, such as cancer, cardiovascular problems, viral and bacterial infections [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0928493114006067#bb0030).

The gas-liquid slug flow, which is characterized by sequences of a gas bubble and a liquid slug, is one of the most important two-phase flow patterns in micro-channel and has been widely applied in chemical and [electronic chip](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary-sciences/chips- electronics "Learn more about electronic chip from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") cooling industry [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0010). Owing to its low axial back mixing, narrow [residence time distribution](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/residence-time-distribution "Learn more about residence time distribution from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") (RTD) and also high mass and heat transfer intensified by the internal circulation in single slugs, the slug flow has been proven as an ideal flow regime for improving the reaction performance [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0020). To date, the gas-liquid slug flow process has been largely studied from multiple aspects, including the gas bubble and liquid slug length [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0025), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0030), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0035), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0040), the liquid film thickness around bubbles [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0045), [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0050), [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0055), the phase distribution [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0060), [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0065), [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0070), the pressure drop [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0075), [[16]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0080) and the mass transfer [[17]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0085), [[18]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0090), [[19]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0095). The characteristics of bubbles and liquid slugs, the lengths of which are mainly affected by the gas bubble generation process at the junction, have a significant impact on the gas-liquid transport and reaction [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0025). The thickness of liquid film, which is significantly influenced by the inertia, is considered as a function of the capillary number [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0050). The overall mass transfer coefficient in the liquid side is found experimentally to be related to flow parameters, such as bubble velocity and bubble length [[17]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S138589472100646X#b0085). However, most of previous researches deal with empirical regulation of gas- liquid [flow characteristics](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and- planetary-sciences/flow-characteristics "Learn more about flow characteristics from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), while the method to precisely control the slug flow pattern has seldom been reported.

S/W/O compound droplets have wide applications in many fields such as the pharmaceutical industry, [bioreactors](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/biochemical-reactor "Learn more about bioreactors from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") and inertial confinement fusion (ICF) experiments ([Sefton et al., 2000](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250917306656#b0115), [Khademhosseini et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250917306656#b0050), [Taly et al., 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250917306656#b0140), [Shum et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250917306656#b0125), [Norimatsu et al., 2002](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250917306656#b0090), [Letts et al., 1995](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250917306656#b0055), [Norimatsu et al., 1999](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250917306656#b0095), [Cook, 1995](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250917306656#b0010)). For example, PS-PVA double-layer shells, adopted as fuel container, in ICF experiments are always prepared by solidifying the S/W/O compound droplets. At present, the common way to fabricate S/W/O compound droplets is through stirring method. However, wide-size distribution and poor repeatability hampered the wide use of this method. Therefore, a microfluidic device with a T-junction is proposed to fabricate S/W/O compound droplets.

Increasing ecological awareness resulted in fast development of green chemistry in recent years [[[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0015)], and establishing new solvent system is important for realizing clean and sustainable chemical process [[[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0025), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0030)]. The mixture of CO2/Ionic liquid (IL) is a new biphasic system that is able to be used for separation and purification of fine chemicals and natural products [[[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0035), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0040)]. In this system, IL has the advantages of low volatility, high thermal stability and excellent ionic conductivity [[[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0045), [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0050)], which are favorable for chemical reaction and extraction separation. [Carbon dioxide](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical-engineering/carbon- dioxide "Learn more about Carbon dioxide from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") (CO2), being another environmentally benign media, exhibits tunable physical and chemical properties from gas phase to [supercritical](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/supercritical "Learn more about supercritical from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") phase with the variation of temperature and pressure [[[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0055), [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0060)]. More interestingly, CO2 dissolves in many IL, but the IL hardly goes to the bulk CO2 phase. Therefore, the supercritical CO2/IL (ScCO2/IL) has asymmetrical solubility. ScCO2 can be used to extract non-polar organics from ILs without any cross-contamination [[[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0065), [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0070)], and ILs can also be used to capture CO2 from high pressure natural gas and post-combustion flue gas [[[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0075), [[16]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270117312941#bib0080)].

Micro-fluidic systems that generate emulsions of liquid droplets suspended in an outer immiscible liquid have recently received considerable attention due to their biological and chemical application implication ([Kobayashi et al., 2001](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912006033#bib11), [Thorsen et al., 2001](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912006033#bib21), [Garstecki et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912006033#bib6), [Christopher and Anna, 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912006033#bib3), [Teh et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912006033#bib20), [Van Steijn et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912006033#bib23), [Van Steijn et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912006033#bib24)). In one important application using these systems, a single liquid droplet produced can encapsulate one single cell in the droplet and act as a single chemical and biological reactor. Specifically, cell encapsulation can protect the cell from the effect of the shear stress induced by the outer liquid and facilitate the performance of the testing function intended for the encapsulated cell. Although droplet-based micro-fluidic devices have been available and have been developed for such system applications, in-depth understanding of the dynamics of mono-dispersed droplet formation and its associated single droplet reactor performance is still limited.

Controlling the interfacial area and enhancing the mass transfer in reactive multiphase flows is of great importance in chemical engineering. The use of micro-channels in the Taylor flow regime is one of the possible ways to achieve this goal for G–L mass transfer-limited reactive systems through a careful control of the G–L interface and flow pattern at a local scale [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894710007266#bib0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894710007266#bib0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894710007266#bib0015).

The processing of complex fluids occurs in many engineering applications and in biomedical analysis. Efficiency of such processes can be crucially dependent on the rheology of the fluid. Viscous parameters can affect the texture or appearance of a fluid, and also they can determine the shelf-life stability of a product. At present, the monitoring of viscous parameters requires samples to be taken manually and then analyzed in a cone-and-plate rheometer, or similar device. The ability to perform online continuous rheological characterization in real-time would permit tighter monitoring and control in a wide range of applications that involve the processing of fluids of non-Newtonian fluids, such as those in the food and beverage [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0001868613000687#bb0005), pharmaceutical [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0001868613000687#bb0010), oil and [lubrication](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/lubrication "Learn more about lubrication from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0001868613000687#bb0015), and high-tech printing industries [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0001868613000687#bb0020). This would lead to a reduction in wastage caused by processes going off spec, and in the level of manual intervention required for product sampling. Currently, no such commercially available device exists that can perform this task efficiently for a broad range of fluids. Quality control is an endpoint test which results in disposal of below spec product. Continuous monitoring would reduce this wastage, potentially completely. Generally the wastage level of a wide range of processes is around 5%. Recently, much attention has been given to the use of flow configurations that yield an information rich data set of measurable flow parameters that can be mapped, through the solution of an inverse problem, to individual constitutive parameters. With the pressure to develop sustainable materials (biomass derived or utilizing waste products) for processing and manufacturing, industry must respond to the greater variability in input [feedstock](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials-science/feedstock "Learn more about feedstock from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") specification [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0001868613000687#bb0025), as well as [material properties](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials-science/materials- property "Learn more about material properties from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") varying during processing, with better control systems. Hence there currently exists a strong driver for online, continuous rheometry.

Monodisperse droplet generation has been widely studied in the [microfluidic](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/microfluidics "Learn more about microfluidic from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") systems, which is of great importance to be applied in chemical, medical and biological research [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424715300947#bib0135), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424715300947#bib0140), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424715300947#bib0145), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424715300947#bib0150), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424715300947#bib0155), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424715300947#bib0160). To the best of our knowledge, in syringe-pump-driven microfluidic systems, there are some periodic fluctuations of the [flow rates](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/flow-kinetics "Learn more about flow rates from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") which are induced by the mechanical oscillation of the pump motor [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424715300947#bib0165), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424715300947#bib0170). As a result, the volume of individual droplets is also varying in time, with a low frequency ranging from 0.01 Hz to 0.1 Hz [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424715300947#bib0170), [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424715300947#bib0175). In addition, there is some limitation of the dynamic response of the syringe- pump-driven microfluidic systems [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424715300947#bib0180), and it takes several minutes or even one hour for the flow rate of the [syringe pump](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/syringe-pump "Learn more about syringe pump from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") to become steady.

In the continuously growing field of microfluidics, micro-droplet flow, without a doubt, is one of the most attractive and promising subcategories. Apart from the general advantages of microfluidics such as reduced reagent consumption and decreased mass and heat transfer distance, micro-droplet system provides isolated environment with additional internal circulation, which makes those discrete droplets excellent parallel reactors [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894717315838#b0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894717315838#b0010). Besides, with the development of [auxiliary](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/auxiliaries "Learn more about auxiliary from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") tools and techniques in mechanical, electrical and other areas, the manipulation of droplets (coalescence, splitting, mixing, sorting, etc.) has become more and more simple and versatile, which greatly expanded the applications of droplet microfluidics. Therefore, literature has reported micro-droplet being applied in high-throughput bio(chemical) analysis[[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894717315838#b0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894717315838#b0020), protein crystallization [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894717315838#b0025), drug delivery [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894717315838#b0030), synthesis of functional [nanomaterials](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/nanomaterial "Learn more about nanomaterials from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894717315838#b0035) and so on.

Over the past two decades, significant progress has been made in the development of microfluidic devices and their applications for microchemical technology, biotechnology, microelectromechanical system (MEMS) and micrototal analysis system (μTAS) technologies ([Kreutzer et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib20); [Yan et al., 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib36)). Multiphase flows, especially two-phase flows occur frequently in these applications. For example, liquid–liquid or gas–liquid two-phase flows have countless applications in microchemical technology ([Kreutzer et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib20); [Günther et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib16); [Hessel et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib17); [Zhang et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib39); [Su et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib27); [Steegmans et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib26)), and materials synthesis ([Yen et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib38)). For all of these applications, it is vital to control and predict flow behaviors. In microfluidic systems, bubbles or droplets coalesce rarely each other. So, major phenomena occur in the region of the generation of bubbles and droplets. In recent years, great effort has been devoted to exploring the formation of bubbles and droplets in microfluidic devices. The popular geometries for the production of bubbles and droplets are co-flowing ([Hong and Wang, 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib18); [Xiong et al., 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib33)) and hydrodynamic flow-focusing devices ([Anna et al., 2003](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib2); [Cubaud and Ho, 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib5); [Funfschilling et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib12); [Fu et al., 2009a](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib10)), T and Y-junctions based on the cross-flowing rupture technique ([Garstecki et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib13); [Link et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib22)), and geometry-dominated devices ([Yasuno et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib37)). Highly uniform bubbles and droplets can be generated with these methods. However, the bubble formation mechanisms depend significantly on the geometry of microfluidic devices ([Abate et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib1)). For co-flowing devices and hydrodynamic flow-focusing devices, the bubble or droplet formation mechanism is mainly controlled by the gas and liquid inertia, but not the capillarity ([Cubaud et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib6); [Garstecki et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib15); [Dollet et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib8); [Fu et al., 2009b](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib11)). The bubble size in the geometry-dominated breakup technique increases with the increase of viscosity of the continuous phase; but independent of surface tension and flow rates ([Yasuno et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib37)). In T and Y-junctions, the formation of bubbles or droplets could be controlled by the ratio of gas/liquid flow rate or the capillary number, or both of them ([Christopher et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib4); [de Menech et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib7); [Garstecki et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib13); [Thorsen et al., 2001](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib29); [Xu et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250910001600#bib35)).

The flow patterns generated by gas–liquid distributors for mini-scale contactors and reactor systems (diameter, _d_ ∼ 1 mm) have been investigated extensively in the past for a variety of cross-sectional geometrical shapes and lengths ([Suo and Griffith, 1964](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0130), [Barnea et al., 1983](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0025), [Damianides and Westwater, 1988](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0040), [Barajas and Panton, 1993](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0020), [Fukano and Kariyasaki, 1993](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0050), [Mishima et al., 1995](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0105), [Mishima and Hibiki, 1996](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0100), [Triplett et al., 1999a](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0145), [Coleman and Garimella, 1999](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0030), [Shekarriz, 2000](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0125), [Yang and Shieh, 2001](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0195), [Zhao and Bi, 2001](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0200), [Akbar et al., 2003](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0005)). While conducted with model fluids, air and water, these studies are often extended to process fluids for engineering applications. Fundamental studies of this nature usually produce two-phase flow regime maps and semi- analytically determined regime transitions, providing insight into the hydraulic behaviour and heat and mass transfer properties of two-phase mixtures flowing through a straight channel ([Triplett et al., 1999b](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0150), [Kawahara et al., 2002](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0070), [Angeli and Gavriilidis, 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0010), [Niu et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S030193221000176X#b0115)). Limited information is available in literature regarding the impact of complex downstream flow configurations on the flow patterns formed initially. With the continued development of new applications for process flow systems at this scale, the incorporation of downstream phase contactors that enhance heat and mass transfer is inevitable.

Gold nanomaterials (Au NMs) are the most widely studied nanomaterials owing to their unique physicochemical, optical, and biological properties since their first colloidal synthesis ([Dreaden et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250923008291#b0035), [Mao et al., 2020](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250923008291#b0135)). Particularly in biomedical applications, Au NMs-enabled nanomedicine allows simultaneous targeting, diagnosis, therapy, and their functionality can be modified according to the patient demand or diseases ([Dreaden et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250923008291#b0035), [Yao et al., 2020](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250923008291#b0230)). For example, their small size allows them to selectively concentrate on the tumour/inflammation site and enter into cells more rapidly than that of small molecules, and they can preferentially perturb and alter/modify the cellular processes ([Zhang et al., 2020](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250923008291#b0245)). The photophysical properties of the Au NMs favour their usage in biodiagnostic assays ([Wei et al., 2019](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250923008291#b0205)). Due to their easy surface modification, it acts as artificial antibodies, and their binding efficiency can be tuned by controlling the number of binding ligands ([Dreaden et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250923008291#b0035)). Because of their excellent photothermal properties, it allows thermal ablation of tumour cells or wound tissues ([Yan et al., 2021](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250923008291#b0225)). Each biomedical application demands the synthesis of anisotropic Au NMs with desired features ([Illath et al., 2022](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250923008291#b0080)); however, conventional batch synthesis makes it difficult to achieve controlled synthesis due to the lack of control in the reaction kinetics ([Illath et al., 2023](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250923008291#b0085)).

The formation and controlling of microdroplets using two or more immiscible fluids are observed in various droplet-based [microfluidic](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/microfluidics "Learn more about microfluidic from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") devices [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732221025332#b0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732221025332#b0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732221025332#b0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732221025332#b0020). The ability to produce monodispersed microdroplets in such devices has facilitated their widespread applications in numerous fields ranging from food processing [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732221025332#b0025), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732221025332#b0030), medical diagnosis [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732221025332#b0035), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732221025332#b0040) to more intricate drug delivery [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732221025332#b0045), [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732221025332#b0050) processes wherein each microdroplet serve as a separate [compartment](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/physics-and- astronomy/compartments "Learn more about compartment from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") for carrying out biological and chemical reactions [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732221025332#b0055), [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732221025332#b0060). Due to a large surface-area-to-volume ratio, these micro-reactors enhance mixing, significantly reducing reaction time [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732221025332#b0065). Further, an inherent ability of the droplet-based microfluidic system is that it can enclose a sample within a suspending liquid eliminating the problems associated with evaporation or cross-contamination between two or more samples [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732221025332#b0070), [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732221025332#b0075). The droplet generation rate and the individual droplet size must be precisely controlled in all the above-mentioned microfluidic applications. To precisely control the droplet generation and their size distribution, it is essential to understand the effects of different operating parameters on droplet formation in a microfluidic device.
