In recent years, the rapid development of micro-manufacturing technology has promoted the wide application of [microfluidics](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidics "Learn more about microfluidics from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") in chemistry, biology, energy, information and other fields [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754620305896#b1), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754620305896#b2). For microfluidics, the miniaturization of the whole process makes it possible to quickly complete the analysis of micro-samples in a more automated, inexpensive and portable way. Multiphase microfluidics based on droplets or bubbles is one of the most important branches that have developed rapidly in microfluidics in recent years. [Microfluidics devices](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidic-device "Learn more about Microfluidics devices from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") capable of generating microdroplets include cross-junction [microchannel](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microchannel "Learn more about microchannel from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754620305896#b3), Y-junction microchannel [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754620305896#b4) and T-junction microchannel [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754620305896#b5), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754620305896#b6), among which T-junction microchannel is most widely used due to its simple structure and convenient operation. The T-junction microchannel has two inlets and one outlet, respectively injected with immiscible [dispersed phase](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/dispersed-phase "Learn more about dispersed phase from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") fluid and continuous phase fluid, and the dispersed phase fluid finally breaks under the transverse shearing action of the continuous phase fluid to form droplets. By controlling parameters such as the flow rate ratio of two phases and surface tension, the size of the generated droplets can be accurately controlled [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754620305896#b7), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754620305896#b8), [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754620305896#b9).

Renewable source of energy such as biodiesel has received a good acceptance worldwide to reduce the dependence on fossil fuels and protect the environment. The common process to produce biodiesel involves the use of triglyceride (TG) either from vegetable or animal oil with alcohol and the basic catalyst (i.e. [potassium hydroxide](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/potassium-hydroxide "Learn more about potassium hydroxide from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), KOH) to produce fatty acid methyl ester (FAME) and glycerol (a byproduct); also known as [transesterification](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/transesterification "Learn more about transesterification from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") process. As the reaction concludes, two distinct phases are formed; the oil phase and the aqueous phase. The oil phase consists of the biodiesel and the unreacted triglycerides while the aqueous phase consists of glycerol and unreacted alcohol. Process intensification can be defined as any [chemical engineering](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/chemical-engineering "Learn more about chemical engineering from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") development that leads to substantially smaller, cleaner, safer, and more energy efficient technology [[1](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270118311310#bib0005)]. Although transesterification has been widely studied, process intensification in biodiesel production is the new trend that run the process continuously, reduce the reaction time and use a lower amount of catalyst [[2](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270118311310#bib0010)]. A simple modular design or ‘plug & play’ microreactor is possible by using a common transparent capillary tube for microchannel, with manifold junctions as the droplet generators. This method is not only fast and easy to assemble, but it also has significant flexibility to change the microchannel design in terms of total length, internal diameter, channel configuration, and number of junction manifolds. This concept has a bright future for the upscaling of microreactor and intensification of biodiesel production [[3](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270118311310#bib0015)].

[Microfluidic](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/microfluidics "Learn more about Microfluidic from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") devices [[1](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0005)] with diverse industrial [[2](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0010),[3](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0015)] and laboratory [[4](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0020),[5](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0025)] applications have been fabricated from different materials [[6](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0030)]. The most common materials are [silicon](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials-science/silicon "Learn more about silicon from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), glass and metals and recently, polymers due to their particular characteristics [[7](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0035),[8](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0040)]. Among different polymers, for the combination of desired properties including optical transparency, chemical stability, nontoxicity, ease of fabrication and low price, polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) has been used for microfluidics with different geometry and sizes [[6](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0030),[9](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0045)]. [Photolithography](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/optical-lithography "Learn more about Photolithography from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [[[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0050), [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0055), [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0060)], [3D printing](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials-science/three- dimensional-printing "Learn more about 3D printing from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") [[[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0065), [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0070), [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0075)], combined methods [[16](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0080),[17](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0085)] and wire-molding [[[18]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0090), [[19]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0095), [[20]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2352492818300977#bib0100)] are amongst the most applicable methods for PDMS microchannels. Many properties of the microchannels depend on the materials that they are made from. For instance, a microchannel made up of glass has different surface properties with that of one with [silicone](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials-science/polysiloxane "Learn more about silicone from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages").

In the past decades, microfluidics has attracted widespread attention in both academia and industry. As a branch of the microfluidics, the droplet-based microfluidics has many advantages, such as large specific surface area and high heat and mass transfer rate, etc. The microdroplets could be regarded as “microreactors”, in which the sample could be mixed and analyzed [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1226086X17303088#bib0005). The sample used at microscale is much less than that at macroscale, which is favored in many biological, medical and chemical researches and applications due to the low cost [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1226086X17303088#bib0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1226086X17303088#bib0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1226086X17303088#bib0020). To achieve these applications, the controllable generation and manipulation of droplets are of essential importance.

In recent years, multiphase microfluidics technique has been widely applied in diverse fields such as analytical chemistry, chemical synthesis, combinatorial analysis, protein crystallization and drug discovery ([Dendukuri and Doyle, 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250914001018#bib8), [Gunther and Jensen, 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250914001018#bib13), [Huebner et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250914001018#bib15), [Li et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250914001018#bib20), [Marre and Jensen, 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250914001018#bib23), [Song et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250914001018#bib26), [Teh et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250914001018#bib27), [Theberge et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250914001018#bib28), [Whitesides, 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250914001018#bib31)). This technique is typically characterized by the transport of two or more immiscible fluids through microchannels with the cross-sectional dimension in the order of 100 μm. The confinement of microchannel wall makes surface force having greater dominance over others such as viscous, inertial or gravitational forces ([Garstecki et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250914001018#bib12), [van Steijn et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250914001018#bib30)).

Due to its wide range of applications such as cell encapsulation [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732216327179#bb0005), microchemical analysis [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732216327179#bb0010), crystallization of proteins [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732216327179#bb0015), [DNA](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/deoxyribonucleic-acid "Learn more about DNA from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") analysis [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732216327179#bb0020) and so on, dropformation in microchannels has been the subject of increased research interest in recent years. Monodispersed drops have been generated using several different methods in micro-fluidic devices including T-junction [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732216327179#bb0025), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732216327179#bb0030), Co-flowing [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732216327179#bb0035), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732216327179#bb0040), cross junction [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167732216327179#bb0045) and so on. Among these geometries, T-junction microchannels are the most widely researched [microfluidic](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/microfluidics "Learn more about microfluidic from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") configuration for drop formation and manipulation due to its simplicity and low fabrication cost.

Recently, much attention has been paid to the application of multiphase microfluidics in chemical reaction and mixing process, emulsion and extraction technology and medicine and materials synthesis ([Günther and Jensen, 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib18), [Kreutzer et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib24), [Mark et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib29)). Bubbles and droplets are frequently encountered in these applications and can be generated or manipulated controllably by dispersed and continuous flows and geometry and size of microchannels. Confinement is believed to be one of the most important parameters that affect the generation or manipulation of bubbles and droplets ([Guillot et al., 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib21)). For example, the bubble formation process in flow-focusing devices can undergo a 2D and/or 3D collapse with regard to the effects of channel aspect ratio on the gaseous thread ([Dollet et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib11)). The breakup of confined bubbles during the formation process at a T-junction is possibly initiated by flowing liquid from the tip of the thread to the neck rather than by the Rayleigh–Plateau instability, when the capillary number is less than 0.01 ([van Steijn et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib34)). The geometry of microfluidic device is also a major parameter affecting the formation or manipulation of bubbles and droplets ([Abate et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib1), [Calderon et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib4), [Calderon et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib6), [Eshpuniyani et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib12), [Schindler and Ajdari, 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib31)). The formation mechanism of bubbles and droplets is different in various microfluidic geometries: flow-focusing cross-junction, T-junction and Y-junction ([Garstecki et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib19), [Garstecki et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib20), [Steegmans et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib32)). Several special devices were designed to produce droplet pairs and [double emulsions](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical-engineering/multiple- emulsion "Learn more about double emulsions from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), containing some simple microfluidic elements ([Baroud et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib2), [Cristobal et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib8), [Frenz et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib15), [Lao et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911003733#bib25)).

The stability of droplet formation is of great importance for droplet [microfluidics](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/microfluidics "Learn more about microfluidics from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [[[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0020)]. To date, droplet-based microfluidic systems are being applied for the interdisciplinary research, which includes particle synthesis [[5](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0025),[6](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0030)], chemical reactions [[[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0035), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0040), [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0045), [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0050)] and biomedical analysis [[[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0055), [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0060), [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0065), [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0070)]. For droplet microfluidic systems, the dynamic process of droplet formation can induce instability of the microfluidic flows, which will lead to the periodic fluctuations of the droplet velocity [[15](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0075),[16](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0080)] and the [droplet size](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/droplet-size "Learn more about droplet size from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [[17](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0085)]. Especially, the time-varying pressures in a T-junction microdroplet generator have been investigated theoretically and experimentally during drop formation, and [pressure oscillations](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/physics-and- astronomy/pressure-oscillation "Learn more about pressure oscillations from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") can be observed at the T-junctions for each period of droplet production [[18](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0090),[19](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092442471731364X#bib0095)]. In particular, for both squeezing and dripping regimes of droplet formation, the pressure of the T-junction is a periodic function of time, and the frequency of the pressure fluctuations increases with the [Capillary number](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/capillary-number "Learn more about Capillary number from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages").

In the past 20 years, the modularization, miniaturization and integration of the [process engineering](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/process-engineering "Learn more about process engineering from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") have attracted increasing attention. Microfluidic equipment and its application in microchemical have achieved great advancement [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954121001075#b0005). In industry, the microfluidic technology has been widely used in [emulsification](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/emulsification "Learn more about emulsification from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), drug encapsulation, material synthesis, crystallization and chemical reactions due to its high efficiency of mass and heat transfer, easy control, environmental protection and high process safety [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954121001075#b0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954121001075#b0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954121001075#b0020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954121001075#b0025), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954121001075#b0030), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954121001075#b0035), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954121001075#b0040). Liquid-liquid two-phase flow in microchannels is an important branch for the research and application of microfluidic technology. The droplet coalescence of different viscosities could control quantitatively the processes of chemical reaction [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954121001075#b0045), mixing [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954121001075#b0050) and mass transfer [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954121001075#b0055), such as biochemical reaction based on microdroplets including the synthesis process of nanoions, which requires the coalescence of two droplets with different properties to achieve good mixing effect. Therefore, the fully understanding on the coalescence of two droplet with different viscosities is a basic requirement for industrial application.

Rapidly developed [micro fabrication](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/microfabrication "Learn more about micro fabrication from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") techniques have facilitated a broad range of microfluidic applications in biological and chemical researches and associated industries. Microdroplet technology is regarded as a promising paradigm for biological and chemical analyses, and each droplet acted as an individual chemical reactor. There has been growing interest in droplet based microfluidic systems because of the advantage in transporting and mixing process. During the last decade, the process of droplet formation in a T-junction has received significant attention ([Stone et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912005672#bib17), [Cramer et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912005672#bib2), [Wu et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912005672#bib23), [DeMenech et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912005672#bib4), [Xu et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912005672#bib24), [van der Zwan et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912005672#bib22), [Zheng and Ismagilov, 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912005672#bib25); Zheng and Ismagilov, 2005).

The characteristics of [chemical engineering](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/chemical-engineering "Learn more about chemical engineering from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") in microscale have been developing very fast within the last decade ([Kashid et al., 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912006069#bib14), [Kreutzer et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912006069#bib18), [Zhao et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912006069#bib39)). Their extremely large surface-to-volume ratio and the short transport path in microchannels can enhance heat and mass transfer dramatically, which make them ideal candidates for heat exchangers and microreactors. In addition, scale-up is achieved by simple replication of microreactor units. The numbering-up mode can eliminate costly reactor redesign and pilot plant experiments, and shorten the research and development time from lab to industrial production. All above advantages could provide many potential opportunities in chemical process intensification and miniaturization development, especially for multiphase systems, such as gas–liquid, liquid–liquid, gas–liquid–solid, etc. ([Abdallah et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912006069#bib1), [Chen et al., 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912006069#bib5), [Kawahara et al., 2002](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912006069#bib15), [Zhao et al., 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912006069#bib40)).

Droplet-based microfluidics has become an attractive platform for fundamental or technical research in the fields of chemistry ([Dressler et al.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0035)), biology ([Bai et al., 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0015)) and physics ([Tabeling, 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0115)). In microfluidic devices, droplets isolate minute quantities of one fluid from a second immiscible fluid ([Chiu and Lorenz](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0020), [Chiu et al.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0025), [Thorsen et al.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0130)), so that chemical or biological agents can be well-confined and the dispersion from the droplet to the external phase is under control ([Link et al.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0070), [Salkin et al.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0085), [Schiller et al., 2015](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0090)). To explore the full potential of droplet-based microfluidics, many technologies have been developed to generate, manipulate and functionalize droplets ([Garstecki et al.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0050), [Tran et al.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0145), [Wang et al.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0150)). The manipulations performed on droplets in microfluidic devices include droplet breakup, fusion and sorting ([Ahmadi et al., 2019](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0005), [Lan et al.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0060), [Simon and Lee, 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0100)). Among them, droplet breakup allows volume and chemical concentration of each droplet to be further adjusted after their generations ([Fukuyama and Hibara](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0045), [Tan et al.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0120), [Tan et al.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250920303882#b0125)), which will facilitate the applications of droplets as microreactors.

The understanding of physical phenomena on a micro and nanoscale in fluid mechanic has been strongly improved during the last decade thanks to the development of miniature devices (e.g., reactors, mixers, etc.). Indeed, microfluidics are relevant in many fields of industrial and practical applications, such as in food processing, automotive industry and medicine, to name but a few. For instance, microfluidic devices used in [microencapsulation](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/microencapsulation "Learn more about microencapsulation from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") and [emulsification](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/emulsification "Learn more about emulsification from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") processes have been undertaken in biotechnology and microchemistry. In thermal field, the calibration of a bubble or a droplet allows to overcome well-controlled bubble or droplet train in order to improve the transfers of heat and mass. Monolith honeycomb catalyst structures are widespread in single phase use in automotive catalyst converters and more recently in [multiphase reactor](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical-engineering/multiphase- reactor "Learn more about multiphase reactor from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") applications. Efficient microfluidic systems, such as a micromixing portable device made of a network of microchannels, were also performed by lithography for bioanalytical systems which need a substantial number of components that is not easy to integrate ([Garstecki et al., 2006a](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912002515#bib15)). T-junction is used in this portable microfluidic device alongside some entry ports for the analytes, and some filters in which the samples are sucked and some micro-mixers in which the main channel splits into two, the arms of which subsequently recombine. Motivated by the control of droplet traffic inside microsystems, [Engl et al. (2005)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912002515#bib11) studied the water droplet traffic performed by two injections of oil flows downstream, in both arms of the T-junction.

Over recent decades, [microencapsulation](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/microencapsulation "Learn more about microencapsulation from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") technologies have attracted a great deal of interest and now it possesses many potential applications for various fields, such as drug encapsulation, materials synthesis, crystallization and chemical reactions [[[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0025)]. In the applications mentioned above, the liquid phase is usually encapsulated into a continuous phase, by which single droplet (W/O or O/W) and compound droplets (W/O/W or O/W/O) were successfully prepared [[[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0030), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0035), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0040), [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0045)]. However, with the increasing demand and development in the [pharmaceutical industry](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/pharmaceutical- industry "Learn more about pharmaceutical industry from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages"), [bioreactors](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/bioreactor "Learn more about bioreactors from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") and [inertial confinement fusion](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/physics- and-astronomy/inertial-confinement-fusion "Learn more about inertial confinement fusion from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") (ICF) experiment, there is a growing interest in the coating of solid particles with liquid layer, namely fabricating of solid in water in oil (S/W/O) compound droplets [[[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0050), [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0055), [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0060), [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0065), [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0070), [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0075), [[16]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0080), [[17]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0085), [[18]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0090), [[19]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775718304722#bib0095)].

Fluid manipulation has been an important research topic increasing interest in the microfluidic analytical systems. Highly precise micro-pumps or high- voltage power supplies have extensively been used for driving solution flows. Physically driven valves or electric fields have widely been utilized for regulating fluids. Various techniques have been examined and adopted to the fluid manipulation inside microchannels [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0039914009005621#bib1), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0039914009005621#bib2), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0039914009005621#bib3), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0039914009005621#bib4), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0039914009005621#bib5), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0039914009005621#bib6), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0039914009005621#bib7), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0039914009005621#bib8). However, these techniques tend to require expensive instruments and delicate operations. Highly precise techniques are also necessary for fabricating channels including micro-valves, ators, or micro-patterns. The development of simple and easy methods for fluid manipulation helps the practical use of microfluidic systems in wide areas.

The microfluidic technology has attracted increasing attention over the last two decades due to its broad development prospects ([Brown et al., 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915002997#bib4), [Hol and Dekker, 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915002997#bib29), [Nge et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915002997#bib36)). The multiphase microfluidic technique, one of the most important branches of microfluidic technology, is characterized by its ability to continuously produce highly monodisperse droplets or bubbles. Such feature has made the microfluidic technique applied to various domains, such as high throughput screening ([Schudel et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915002997#bib39)), chemical synthesis ([Elvira et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915002997#bib12)), drug development ([Wu et al., 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915002997#bib55)) and crystallization ([Puigmarti-Luis, 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915002997#bib37)).

Over the last decade droplet formation has become a very important area of research due to its wide-ranging applications in science and microprocess engineering. The ability to produce nearly monodispersed microdroplets has numerous applications within microfluidic based lab-on-a-chip devices ([Yap et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib32)). The controlled formation of aqueous phase microdroplets dispersed in a continuous phase fluid has unique advantages as the consumption of reagents is small ([Song et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib24), [Li et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib15)). In particular, a number of important biological molecules can be produced from microdroplet based crystallization processes utilizing small samples of solution. During these processes each microdroplet acts as an individual microreactor in which the aqueous solutions are manipulated at room temperature ([Leng and Salmon, 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib14)). The fine controls possible over the size and shape of these microdroplets are of much importance since they influence the biological and chemical properties of microparticles ([Teh et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib28)). The major advantages of droplet based fluidic systems are the existence of a high surface-to-volume ratio, rapid mixing within the droplet or plug at low Reynolds numbers ([Song et al., 2003](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib25), [Tice et al., 2003](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib30)) and the enclosure of a sample within a suspending liquid, eliminating several problems associated with evaporation and cross contamination between successive samples that are encountered in macroscale systems ([Song et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib24), [Leshansky and Pismen, 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib16)). A number of methods have been developed for droplet formation. These include droplet breakup at a symmetric T-junction ([Leshansky and Pismen, 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib16)) or bifurcation junction ([Jullien et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib11)), flow focussing of a continuous stream of liquid which guides the droplets formed toward the center of the channel ([Anna et al., 2003](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib1), [Tan et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib26)), perpendicular rupturing using a cross-flow microchannel ([Tan et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib27)), and the shearing of the dispersed phase stream by the continuous phase at a T-junction ([Thorsen et al., 2001](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib29), [Nisisako et al., 2002](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib17), [Garstecki et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib8)). [Husny and Cooper-White (2006)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib10) ran a series of experiments to study the effect of elasticity on drop formation in a T-shaped microchannel. They found that the presence of elasticity with low viscosity fluids resulted in the creation of secondary drops of varying sizes. [Zhou et al. (2006)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib34) performed a numerical study of the formation of simple and compound drops in microfluidic flow-focusing devices. They used a finite element scheme with adaptive meshing in a diffuse-interface framework to simulate breakup in coflowing conditions and also to investigate the effects of viscoelasticity in the drop phase. [Davidson et al. (2005)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911004118#bib3) used a volume-of-fluid (VOF) method to predict the dynamics of droplet formation in a microfluidic flow-focusing geometry. They obtained a qualitative comparison between the VOF simulations and experimental observations.

Bubbles/droplets are indispensable in microfluidics in a broad range of applications, such as microchemical technology ([Rajesh and Buwa, 2018](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921005753#b0130), [Derzsi et al., 2016](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921005753#b0025)), biotechnology, space-based systems ([Arias and Montlaur, 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921005753#b0010)); and material synthesis ([Hou et al., 2016](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921005753#b0070)), where they exhibit multiple dynamic behaviors, including flow, breakup, and coalescence in systems ([Anna, 2016](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921005753#b0005), [Fu and Ma, 2015](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921005753#b0035), [Haase, 2016](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921005753#b0060)). The bubble/droplet size, which determines the interface dynamics, flow resistance, and path selection of fluids in microfluidic chips, is a fundamental parameter in these applications and is affected by complex conditions, such as the reaction between the fluid, interface, and walls of channels ([Wang et al., 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921005753#b0165), [Stone, 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921005753#b0140), [Vanapalli et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921005753#b0160)). Therefore, it is vital to predict and control the size of bubbles/droplets and their flow behaviors precisely to achieve stable and controllable performance in these applications.

The production of bubbles in [microfluidic devices](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/microfluidic-device "Learn more about microfluidic devices from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") is widely studied and applied in clinical medicine [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0005), synthesis of new materials [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0010), environmental protection [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0015) with the advantages of precise controllability with the size and shape of bubbles [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0025), high heat and mass transfer efficiency [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0030), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0035). Many studies focus on bubble formation in [Newtonian fluids](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/newtonian-fluid "Learn more about Newtonian fluids from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") with various configurations, the mechanism of bubble formation is controlled by the flow rate ratio of both phases and the capillary number of the liquid phase, the bubble size decreases with the increase of the liquid capillary number, and flow rate ratio of gas and liquid phases [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0040), [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0045), [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0050). In practical industrial applications, non-Newtonian fluids with polymer are usually used as the continuous phase, in which the high extensibility of polymer [molecular chain](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and- planetary-sciences/molecular-chain "Learn more about molecular chain from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") is of great significance in the improvement of oil recovery [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0055), the extraction of high-purity plasma [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0060) and high-speed ink-jet printing [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0065). In this case, it is necessary to explore the effect of [viscoelasticity](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/viscoelasticity "Learn more about viscoelasticity from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") on formation of bubbles or droplets, and most of the related studies focus on the formation of Newtonian droplets in [viscoelastic fluids](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth- and-planetary-sciences/viscoelastic-fluid "Learn more about viscoelastic fluids from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") in flow focusing devices. Gupta and Sbragaglia [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0070) performed numerical simulations to analyze the droplet formation in viscoelastic fluids, and it was found that the effect of elasticity on the liquid–liquid interface was more obvious with the viscoelasticity of the continuous phase. When the droplet was broken periodically, the feedback stress produced by the polymer caused the local deformation of the droplet, and the distribution of the feedback stress was related to the shape and break-up point of the droplet. Derzsi et al., [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0075) presented a comparison between Newtonian fluids and viscoelastic fluids as the continuous phase in a flow-focusing device, and found that viscoelastic fluids can promote the generation of droplets, to produce a smoother dripping - jetting transition, and to reduce the [monodispersity](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/monodispersity "Learn more about monodispersity from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") of droplets by adjusting the viscosity ratio of the dispersed phase to the continuous phase in the jetting pattern more easily. Nooranidoost et al., [[16]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0080) numerically explored the effect of viscoelasticity on flow patterns of droplet formation. It was considered that the viscoelasticity slowed down the transformation of flow patterns, and the size of droplets was sensitive to the Weissenberg number which is related to the relaxation time and deformation rate of polymer molecules in the dripping flow pattern. Yue et al., [[17]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0085) used numerical simulations to investigate the deformation of a single droplet in steady shear flows in viscoelastic fluids. It was found that the viscoelasticity in the continuous phase has stronger inhibition effects on the droplet deformation than that in the dispersed phase, the reason lies in the fact that the acting force of polymer tends to pull the liquid–liquid interface inward. Chung et al., [[18]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0090) found that the shape of droplet is similar to an ellipsoid due to the normal stress difference in viscoelastic fluids, that is, the profile shape of liquid - liquid phases can be controlled by adjusting the characteristics of viscoelastic fluids. In addition, the formation process of bubbles is different from that of droplets. Zhang et al., [[19]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0095) demonstrated that the competition between the interfacial tension and viscous force which closely influences the deformation behavior of the interface between phases. The viscosity ratio of gas and liquid are much smaller than that of liquid and liquid, and the interfacial tension between the gas and liquid is usually larger than that between the liquid and liquid, which causes the different interfacial profile shapes in gas - liquid system and liquid – liquid system. However, compared with the extensive study of droplets, the effect of viscoelasticity on bubble formation has received less attentions. To our best knowledge, only Kim et al., [[20]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0100) showed the effect of viscoelasticity on the shape of bubbles in a flow- focusing microdevice. Bubbles were obviously different from those in Newtonian fluids, due to the normal stress difference between the bubble and the microchannel wall. However, the effects of the viscoelasticity on the bubble formation and the bubble size in microchannels remains unclear, which needs to be explored for the controllable production of bubbles in viscoelastic complex fluids in microfluidics. Moreover, the configuration of microdevices plays a leading role in the flow regimes and force distribution of gas–liquid two- phase flows [[21]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0105). The T-junction is one of the most widely used configurations, and many important tasks such as the formation and distribution of bubbles have been performed in parallelized microchannels with such configuration [[22]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0110), [[23]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0115). However, to the best of our knowledge, the information on the bubble formation in viscoelastic fluids in T-junctions within parallelized microchannels is unrevealed. In this work, on the basis of the investigation of the effect of liquid viscosity on bubble formation in Newtonian fluids in the T-junction microchannel [[24]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0120), [[25]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894721033647#b0125), the elastic factor is introduced to explore the effects of the viscosity and the elasticity of viscoelastic fluids on bubble formation in T-junctions within parallelized microchannels.

Research interest on two-phase flows and their mixing processes in microchannels has increased tremendously in the last decade because of their biochemical applications, applications as micro heat exchangers, etc. ([Thorsen et al., 2001](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932212001413#b0105), [Kreutzer et al., 2005a](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932212001413#b0060), [Kreutzer et al., 2005b](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932212001413#b0065), [Stone et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932212001413#b0100), [Agostini et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932212001413#b0015), [Revellin et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932212001413#b0090), [Cubaud and Ho, 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932212001413#b0030)). In particular, slug flow (Taylor flow), which consists of alternate flows of liquid slugs and gas bubbles (or liquid droplets), is an interesting flow regime in typical flow patterns in microchannels. Recently, numerous studies have contributed to achieving control of the bubble/droplet sizes and an understanding of their dynamics in microchannels ([Garstecki et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932212001413#b0040), [van Steijn et al., 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932212001413#b0120), [van Steijn et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932212001413#b0125), [Leclerc et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932212001413#b0070), [Li et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932212001413#b0080), [Abate et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932212001413#b0010), [Lee et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932212001413#b0075), [Zaloha et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932212001413#b0130)).

Ammoximation of cyclohexanone is an important process to synthesize cyclohexanone oxime, which is a key intermediate in the production of caprolactam, the [monomer](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/monomer "Learn more about monomer from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") for nylon-6 ([Dahlhoff et al., 2001](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250918302501#b0010)). In 1987, a single-step ammoximation process was developed, in which cyclohexanone reacts with ammonia and hydrogen peroxide to form cyclohexanone oxime with the catalysis of titanium silicalite-1 (TS-1). It has been demonstrated that the process on an industrial scale could result in a high yield up to 99% ([Lin et al., 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250918302501#b0055), [Thangaraj et al., 1991](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250918302501#b0085)). In the industrial process, the organic solvent _t_ -butanol is used to improve the reaction performance ([Yip and Hu, 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250918302501#b0135), [Zhao et al., 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250918302501#b0160)). However, the large amount of solvent results in much larger size reactor, environmental drawbacks and very high separation cost. Moreover, it is reported that the by-products generated in _t_ -butanol can cause deactivation of the TS-1 catalyst ([Song et al., 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250918302501#b0080), [Zhang et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250918302501#b0150)). Therefore, it is of great significance to develop an organic solvent-free heterogeneous cyclohexanone ammoximation process.

Drop formation and breakup are ubiquitous in daily life and are usually a basic and necessary processes in many industrial applications including the production of skin care products like shampoo, foods like mayonnaise, oil production like emulsion flooding and drug encapsulation, etc. ([Whitesides, 2016](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219305428#bib0155); [Carrier et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219305428#bib0020); [Dai et al., 2018](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219305428#bib0040), [2019](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219305428#bib0045); [Anton et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219305428#bib0005); [Jia et al., 2019](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219305428#bib0085); [Cao et al., 2019](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219305428#bib0015)). Generally, the high shear processes are applied to produce abundant new drops, for instance, highly efficient mixing and agitation. Unfortunately, these traditional processes are often discontinuous and could lead to a wide [drop size distribution](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/drop-size- distribution "Learn more about drop size distribution from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") over even three orders of magnitude. The [polydispersity](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/polydispersity "Learn more about polydispersity from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") of the [droplet size](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/droplet-size "Learn more about droplet size from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") is usually a undisirable outcome and has a very negative impact on the controllable release of drugs, [shelf life](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/shelf-life "Learn more about shelf life from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") of emulsion products and user experience of cosmetics, therefore, it sacrifices the product quality and debases the value ([Xu et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219305428#bib0180); [Carrier et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219305428#bib0020)).

Droplet microfluidics has been widely applied for medical, biological and chemical research ([Hale et al., 2018](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0045), [Zhang et al., 2020](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0135), [Li et al., 2020](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0075), [Zeng and Fu, 2020](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0125), [Schuler et al., 2016](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0100)). In particular, individual droplets with volume ranging from 1 pL to 100 nL are formed in the microchannels, and the control precision of the droplet size is of significant importance for the applications of droplet microfluidic systems ([Fryd and Mason, 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0015), [Zhan et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0130), [Yang et al., 2020](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0120), [Rane et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0095), [Guo et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0040)).. According to the literature; both flow-rate- and pressure-driven pumping methods have been applied for droplet formation, and the size of the droplets as a function of the flow-rate ratio or pressure ratio is measured experimentally ([Ward et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0105)). In a T-junction microdroplet generator, it was observed that the droplet size is approximately a linear function of the flow-rate ratio while monodisperse droplets are generated at low capillary numbers (Ca⩽0.1) ([Garstecki et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0025), [Glawdel et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0035), [Li et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0070)). Particularly, for a typical geometry of the microchannel, a 10% increase in the pressure ratio will induce nearly 4 fold increase in droplet size, while a 10% increase in the flow-rate ratio can only lead to less than 30% increase in droplet size ([Kebriaei and Basu, 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0060)). Therefore, the droplet size is less sensitive to the variation of the flow- rate ratio compared with that of the pressure ratio, and meanwhile, the control accuracy of the flow rates of the fluids directly affects the stability and the control precision of droplet formation ([Korczyk et al., 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0065)). Besides the T-junctions; the principle of droplet formation has also been studied theoretically and experimentally in a flow-focusing microchannel ([Garstecki et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0020), [Miller et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0080), [Moyle et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0085)). Both for low and high capillary numbers, it is observed that the size of the droplets varies nonlinearly with the flow-rate ratio ([Jung and Oh, 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0055), [Hong and Wang, 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0050)). Especially for high capillary numbers 0.1⩽Ca⩽1.0, the drop size can also change with the viscosity of the fluids ([Nie et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925092100364X#b0090)). Due to the inherent nonlinearity between the droplet size and the flow-rate ratio in the flow-focusing microchannel, the size of droplets can be controlled and predicted more easily in the T-junctions.

Droplet-based microfluidics has got much attraction due to its various applications in diagnostic assays, biosciences, and analytical chemistry [[1](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270122002070#bib0001),[2](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270122002070#bib0002)]. There are some significant benefits for droplet-based microfluidics. One of the advantages is preventing the sample fluids from pollution and chemical reactions by encapsulating them [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270122002070#bib0003). The second advantage is increasing the reaction speed through better mixing of reactants in the droplet [[2](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270122002070#bib0002),[[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270122002070#bib0004), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270122002070#bib0005), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270122002070#bib0006)]. Reducing the cost of operation and increasing the sensitivity, precision, and portability are other advantages of droplet-based microfluidics [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270122002070#bib0007).

Microfluidic applications have been extensively used in a wide variety of fields such as micro-chemical engineering, electronics cooling, and biomedical engineering because of their compact structure, good controllability, and high transport efficiency ([Chen et al., 2019](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921009404#b0045), [Cheng et al., 2021](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921009404#b0050)). The confined two-phase flow in microchannels is always encountered in microfluidic applications, and the manipulation of a two-phase flow is recognised as a typical problem ([Haringa et al., 2019](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921009404#b0080), [Leshansky et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921009404#b0110), [Yang et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921009404#b0245), [Yao et al., 2021](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921009404#b0255)). It is crucial to understand its physical mechanisms to better serve the design and optimisation of microfluidic applications.

At present, the newly discovered medium and high permeability oil fields become less. Tight oil reservoirs attract increasing attention of oil field development [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775722017678#bib1), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775722017678#bib2). Tremendous reserves of tight oil resources exist in the world. However, their pore and throat are narrow and the flowing capacity is poor [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775722017678#bib3), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775722017678#bib4), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775722017678#bib5), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775722017678#bib6). At the same time, the tight reservoir is mainly developed by water injection, which has some problems such as high injection pressure and poor oil displacement efficiency [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775722017678#bib7), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775722017678#bib8). With the development of the nanotechnology, [nanofluid](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/physics-and- astronomy/nanofluid "Learn more about nanofluid from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") has been used in the upstream and downstream of oilfield development. Compared with conventional fluids such as brine and [surfactant](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials-science/surface- active-agent "Learn more about surfactant from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") solutions, nanofluid is composed of [nanoparticles](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/nanoparticle "Learn more about nanoparticles from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), which shows a great potential for enhanced oil recovery [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775722017678#bib9), [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775722017678#bib10), [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775722017678#bib11), [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775722017678#bib12).

The chemical process industry is continuously evolving over the years. Recent research and [technology](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and- planetary-sciences/science-and-technology "Learn more about technology from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") efforts are directed towards developing sustainable technologies thereby maximizing production and minimizing cost & energy consumption and waste generation [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894718325348#b0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894718325348#b0020). The crucial need to develop environmental friendly, energy-efficient and cost- effective chemical processes has given rise to the development of micro- structured reactors and process equipment [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894718325348#b0025), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894718325348#b0030), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894718325348#b0035). Micro-reactors allow to perform chemical reactions in a confinement with characteristic dimensions ranging from 10 to 1000 μm [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894718325348#b0040), [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894718325348#b0045), [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894718325348#b0050). Micro-reactors gain an edge over the conventional reactors (stirred batch vessels) with several advantages, which includes, better safety, improved control of reaction conditions, enhanced mixing, and higher yields. The surface area to volume ratio in micro-reactors is several orders of magnitude higher (≃10,000–50,000 m2/m3) compared to the conventional equipment (≃100–1000 m2/m3) [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894718325348#b0055). As a result, heat and mass transfer rates are significantly higher in micro- channels, leading to improved reaction yield and [selectivity](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/selectivity "Learn more about selectivity from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages"). Due to the reduction in size, a remarkable increase in the interfacial transport phenomena is observed in micro-reactors [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894718325348#b0055), [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894718325348#b0060), [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894718325348#b0065). Moreover, the reduced dimensions up to micro-meter and sub-milli-meter scale and small reaction volume allows to perform the hazardous, highly exothermic and mass transfer limited reactions in [microfluidic devices](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/microfluidic-device "Learn more about microfluidic devices from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894718325348#b0070).

Gas-liquid slug flows are attractive in a broad range of applications, such as in chemical, bio-chemical and material synthesis, drug discovery, medical diagnostics ([Suryawanshi et al., 2018](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/B9780323851596501664#bb0015)). The slug generation mechanism can be divided in different regimes such as squeezing, dripping and jetting, based on the capillary number ([Zhu and Wang, 2016](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/B9780323851596501664#bb0020)). The focus of the present research lies on T-junctions operating in the squeezing regime (cf. [Fig. 1](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/B9780323851596501664#f0010)). The squeezing regime is governed by surface tension forces, making the pinch- off mechanism independent from fluid parameters like viscosity. Extensive work in this area has been done which resulted in models trying to predict the slug size from feed flows and channel geometry. In the present research, experimental validation of the proposed model by [van Steijn et al (2010)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/B9780323851596501664#bb0025) is performed in millimetre scaled channels and channel geometries that have not been tested for this model. Based on the results, the shortcomings of the model are explained and tried to overcome.

[Microfluidic](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidics "Learn more about Microfluidic from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") reactors offer advantages associated with high surface-to-volume ratios, often by several orders of magnitude, compared to those of [macroscale](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/macroscale "Learn more about macroscale from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") devices. Therefore, transfer processes can occur across a greater interfacial surface area, leading to increased heat and mass transfer rates. Consequently, the final equilibrium state may be attained from a lower energy consumption. Fluid behavior on micron scale dimensions is influenced by viscous effects rather than by inertial properties as the flow is essentially laminar, i.e. the [Reynolds number](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/reynolds-number "Learn more about Reynolds number from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), Re < 1 ([Teh et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932213001973#b0160)), with mass transfer and mixing processes being dominated by diffusion rather than by convection as in the macroscale case. In the case of single phase flow in a [microchannel](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microchannel "Learn more about microchannel from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), the dispersion of solutes occurs along the length of the channel, which can lead to dilution and cross-contamination of injected samples. The confinement of chemical mixtures inside [liquid droplets](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/liquid-droplet "Learn more about liquid droplets from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), or plugs, surrounded by an immiscible fluid in a microchannel has been shown to overcome these problems ([Song et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932213001973#b0145), [Leshansky and Pismen, 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932213001973#b0085)). More efficient transverse mass and [heat transfer rates](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/heat-transfer-rate "Learn more about heat transfer rates from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") may be achieved due to the presence of [recirculation zones](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/recirculation-zone "Learn more about recirculation zones from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") within the liquid plugs.

Bubbles or droplets are always encountered in the application of microfluidics and have been received much attention in recent years [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270111000687#bib0030), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0255270111000687#bib0035). Highly uniform bubbles and droplets can be generated with these devices.
