The production of two-phase liquid–liquid drop and plug flow in microchannels has become an important hallmark of microfluidic research because of its robust application to different industries including the biotechnology, pharmaceutical and chemical industries [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711006000#bib0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711006000#bib0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711006000#bib0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711006000#bib0020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711006000#bib0025). Liquid–liquid two-phase flows also provide unique opportunities for studying novel fluid dynamic and interfacial phenomena [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711006000#bib0030), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711006000#bib0035), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711006000#bib0040). Numerous studies have been conducted in the past on different aspects of two- phase flows of immiscible liquids in various microfluidic channel geometries including the T-shaped, cross-flow, flow focusing and head-on junctions [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711006000#bib0045), [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711006000#bib0050), [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711006000#bib0055), [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711006000#bib0060), [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711006000#bib0065), [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711006000#bib0070).

With the advancement in applications of clean energy, renewables and energy storage [[[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib1), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib2), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib3), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib4), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib5)], [hydrogen production](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/hydrogen- production "Learn more about hydrogen production from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") [[[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib6), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib7), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib8)], storage and transportation facilities are key links in the [hydrogen economy](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/hydrogen-economy "Learn more about hydrogen economy from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"). Micro-sized and integrated actuators gradually play an important role for hydrogen production [[9](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib9),[10](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib10)], chemical and process engineering, energy science, biotechnology and pharmaceutical technology [[11](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib11),[12](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib12)]. For hydrogen production in [microreactors](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microreactor "Learn more about microreactors from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), gas releasing processes from a liquid reactant are of a potential to enable static and mobile [hydrogen storage](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/hydrogen-storage "Learn more about hydrogen storage from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") and [hydrogen utilization](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/hydrogen- utilization "Learn more about hydrogen utilization from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") in fuel cells. Thus, gas-liquid flow is important concerning reaction [[13](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib13)], sorting, evaluation and mixing in these [microfluidic](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidics "Learn more about microfluidic from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") actuators, which takes advantage of the high specific [interfacial area](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/interfacial-area "Learn more about interfacial area from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") and high heat and mass transfer rates at [microscale](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microscale "Learn more about microscale from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [[[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib12), [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib13), [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib14), [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib15), [[16]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib16)]. Therefore, pinch-off dynamics during the process of [bubble breakup](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/bubble-breakup "Learn more about bubble breakup from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") and formation [[18](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib18)] at [microchannel](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microchannel "Learn more about microchannel from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") junctions has aroused great concern [[12](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib12),[[19]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib19), [[20]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib20), [[21]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib21), [[22]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib22)]. When the interface deforms at the junction, there are two major periods i.e., linear and nonlinear collapses [[23](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib23)]. Research focus is mainly focused on the nonlinear collapse, also termed as the pinch-off period where the bubble interface detaches from channel walls [[24](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib24),[25](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360319921029037#bib25)], because it demonstrates quite dynamic and unique characteristics.

In the field of fluid dynamics, the study on Taylor flow is gaining popularity, especially in designing microchannels and microreactors ([Al- Rawashdeh et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib2), [Gao et al., 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib10), [Kashid et al., 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib18), [Lang et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib20), [Su et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib27)). In Taylor flow, the generation of bubble is highly monodispersed with an equal space between slug ([Fries et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib6), [Ganapathy et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib9)). Besides, due to the recirculating flows in liquid slug and a thin liquid film between the wall and bubble, both the mass transfer and heat transfer between the slug, the wall and the bubble are enhanced in Taylor flow ([Kashid et al., 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib17), [Kashid et al., 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib18)). In order to fully utilize the strengths of Taylor flow, bubbles with uniform and controllable sizes should be generated in microchannels or microreactors. Therefore, many efforts have been made to study the dynamics of bubble formation process and to control bubble size ([Garstecki et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib11), [Gupta et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib13), [Van Steijn et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib29), [Xu et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib36)). However, these studies on Taylor flow were mainly based on steady state flows with a uniform bubble size. At some operation conditions, significant fluctuations and disturbances might cause non-uniform bubbles in Taylor flow ([Abadie et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib1), [Ide et al., 2009](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib16), [Qian and Lawal, 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib22), [Santos and Kawaji, 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib25), [Yamamoto and Ogata, 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib39)). Those non-uniform bubbles with uneven sizes and surface areas will jeopardize a precise control of heat transfer, mass transfer and reaction in microchannels and microreactors ([Houshmand and Peles, 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib15), [Sobieszuk et al., 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib26)), and will lead to a lower conversion rate ([Al-Rawashdeh et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib2)) and an inaccurate measurement of reaction kinetics ([Li et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib21)). Moreover, this undesirable phenomenon will also cause disordered splits ([Hoang et al., 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib14)), coalescence ([Wu et al., 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib35)) and array storage ([Xu et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib38)) for microfluidic. Therefore, bubble uniformity is critical to taking advantage of Taylor flow in microreactors and microfluidics, and the acceptable deviation of bubble size normally is smaller than 5–10% in practice ([Fries et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib6), [Yue et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib41), [Yue et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib42), [Al-Rawashdeh et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915000937#bib2)).

In early 1990s, the concept of miniaturization led to the emergence of microfluidic technology ([Manz et al., 1990](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib26)). Ever since, there has been growing interest and development in academic research and practical applications of microfluidics ([Dittrich and Manz, 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib10), [G Nther and Jensen, 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib16), [Jensen, 2001](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib21), [Whitesides, 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib42), [Zhao, 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib46)). The enthusiasm on micro-structured reactors is mainly attributed to their superior features compared to the macro-counterparts, such as fast mass/heat transfer, improved intrinsic safety and easiness of numbering up. One sub- category of microfluidics is droplet-based microfluidics, which deals with two or more immiscible fluids and involves the generation and manipulation of discrete droplets in microdevices ([Teh et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib36), [Casadevall I Solvas and DeMello, 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib32)). Compared to other forms of microfluidics, droplet-based microfluidics has larger surface area to volume ratio and additional inner vortex, both of which are beneficial to the enhanced mixing and mass transfer ([Song et al., 2003](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib34), [Kinoshita et al., 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib22), [Rhee and Burns, 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib29)). Meanwhile, since the droplets can be manipulated flexibly in elaborately fabricated microdevices, each independent droplet is analogous to a tiny batch reactor in which mixing, mass transfer, reaction, and separation can be controlled precisely ([Chen et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib4), [Yang et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib45)). Therefore, droplet-based microfluidics has become a hotspot of research with great potential to be applied in chemical reaction, molecular detection, drug delivery, diagnostic, cell biology, and so on ([Song et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib33), [Du et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib11), [Benz et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib2), [Zhao, 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib46), [Bardiya et al., 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib1)). More information about droplet manipulation and their versatile applications can be referred to related reviews (Casadevall I [Solvas and DeMello, 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib32); [Rosenfeld et al., 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib30); [Chou et al., 2015](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250916300586#bib5)).

Microdroplet technology has been developed [[1](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424721003824#bib0005),[2](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424721003824#bib0010)] and applied in various fields such as [chemistry](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/chemistry "Learn more about chemistry from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") and biochemistry [[[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424721003824#bib0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424721003824#bib0020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424721003824#bib0025), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424721003824#bib0030)]. In particular, in the field of biochemistry, technology for encapsulating cells and [organelles](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/physics-and- astronomy/organelle "Learn more about organelles from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") individually in microdroplets and culturing them has been attracting attention [[3](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424721003824#bib0015),[4](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424721003824#bib0020),[6](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924424721003824#bib0030)]. Given that the size of cells and organelles is approximately 2–30 μm, the size of the droplet needs to be about 10–50 μm in diameter. Therefore, we conducted this fundamental research aimed at stably producing droplets of around 10 μm in size.

Multivesiculated polyester particles (MVPs) have been used in paint industry as opacifying agents for partial substitution of costly titanium dioxide [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894713010474#b0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894713010474#b0010). Opacity is obtained by light refraction within air-filled internal voids, thanks to the large difference in [refractive indexes](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/refractivity "Learn more about refractive indexes from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") (RI) between polymer walls (RI of ca. 1.6) and air (RI ca. 1.0). The particles are obtained by crosslinking a w/o/w [double emulsion](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/multiple-emulsion "Learn more about double emulsion from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") produced in a two-step [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894713010474#b0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894713010474#b0020) or one-step [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894713010474#b0005), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894713010474#b0025) process in a batch reactor. In the two-step process, water is emulsified in an organic phase made of unsaturated polyester dissolved in [styrene](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/styrene "Learn more about styrene from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), and the resulting w/o emulsion is dispersed in an aqueous solution of protective colloids. In the one-step process, on the other hand, the organic phase is dispersed in the aqueous phase, and water then diffuses into the droplets to form the final double emulsion. In both cases, the w/o emulsion is stabilized by hydrophilic acid–base ion-pairs formed by neutralization of the terminal polyester carboxylic groups with an added amine – diethylenetriamine is used in all literature. In a previous work [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894713010474#b0030) we have shown that these [carboxylate](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/carboxylate "Learn more about carboxylate from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") salts also play a fundamental role on the stabilization of the o/w emulsion, due to placement of a fraction of the end groups at the outer oil–water interface, as illustrated in [Fig. 1](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894713010474#f0005)a. This electrostatic stabilization mechanism is similar to the existent in waterborne [polyurethane](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/polyurethane "Learn more about polyurethane from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") dispersions (PUDs), which contain pendant neutralized carboxylic groups at the surface [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894713010474#b0035). Upon chemical crosslinking of the polyester–styrene organic phase, via [radical polymerization](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/free-radical-polymerization "Learn more about radical polymerization from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), an aqueous dispersion of highly vesiculated solid particles is obtained. [Fig. 1](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894713010474#f0005)b presents a SEM image depicting particles produced in the conventional [batch process](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/batch-process "Learn more about batch process from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), showing the internal structure obtained after drying [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894713010474#b0040). Numerous alveoli separated by thin polymer walls are visible. Average particle sizes below 10 μm are desired when incorporation in non-matte coatings is intended.

Droplet-based [microfluidic devices](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidic-device "Learn more about microfluidic devices from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0017931015007322#b0005) have gained a long-standing interest over the past two decades due to their enormous potential in scientific research and [engineering applications](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/engineering- application "Learn more about engineering applications from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") ranging from chemical reactions [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0017931015007322#b0010), biotechnology [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0017931015007322#b0015), flow and heat transfer in micro-electromechanical system (MEMS) [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0017931015007322#b0020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0017931015007322#b0025). One of the commonly used microfluidic devices for droplet formation is the T-junction depicted schematically in [Fig. 1](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0017931015007322#f0005), in which the continuous phase and the [dispersed phase](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/dispersed-phase "Learn more about dispersed phase from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") fluids flow into the main channel and the lateral channel respectively, and meet at the perpendicular junction. In a T-junction, droplets are generated by an interface induced instability resulting from the competition among three forces, i.e., the local [viscous stresses](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/viscous-stress "Learn more about viscous stresses from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") acting to deform the liquid interface, the increased upstream pressure caused by the obstruction of the junction as the tip of the dispersed phase grows, and the capillary pressure acting to resist the deformation. T-junctions are widely used in droplet-based microfluidics because of the ease in fabrication and operation, as well as the ability for producing uniform droplets of the required volume, frequency and [monodispersity](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/monodispersity "Learn more about monodispersity from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages").

Since the development of devices for inkjet printer in the ‘50s, [microfluidic](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/microfluidics "Learn more about microfluidic from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") technology has been addressed as a highly performant and reliable tool for a wide range of applications, such as chemical and biological analysis and sensing [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0005). Although the microfluidics devices are compact and have a reduced size, in most of the cases they still require bulky and extra optical set-ups to investigate and detect the fluid and [dispersed phases](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/dispersed-phase "Learn more about dispersed phases from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") within, such as microscopes and imaging processes. In particular, fast sensing applications typically require expensive fast cameras, large data storage and need long post processing analysis, which make unfeasible a real- time sensing. This lack of integration and portability between the microfluidic device and the optical detection set-up is one of the main issue for non-massive [commercialization](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/commercialisation "Learn more about commercialization from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") of microfluidic devices, thus keeping most of the prototypes just at a proof-of-concept. For these reasons, increasing attempts to integrate multiple stages on the same substrate have been proposed. Among others, the realization of an optical stage, able to detect and identify the flow of objects inside micro-channels has particular interest especially in the field of particle sensing and [actuation](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/actuation "Learn more about actuation from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"). Many solutions have been tested to substitute imaging techniques: the embedding of [optical fibers](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/optical- fiber "Learn more about optical fibers from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") in polymeric based device [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0025), the integration of [waveguide](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/waveguide "Learn more about waveguide from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") by means of micro-lenses to focus the light in the middle of the [fluidic](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/fluidics "Learn more about fluidic from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") channels [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0030), the integration of localized LED sources [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0035), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0040) or [photodiodes](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/photodiode "Learn more about photodiodes from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0040), [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0045), and capacitive sensing [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0050), [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0055), [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0060), [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0065), [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0070), [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0075) or thermal sensing [[16]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0080) by means of electrode are the most investigated. However, each of them has severe drawbacks: for example, electrodes exhibit degradation problems and may be too invasive; while the fiber coupling and the combination of waveguide with lenses suffer for very low reproducibility in the fabrication, like aligning problems. Some tests have been tried to integrate a waveguide with a microfluidic channel [[17]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0085), [[18]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0090), [[19]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925400518318513#bib0095), but in channels roughness did not allow a perfect coupling, maintaining align problem.

Flows in small channels, with dimensions less than 1 mm, have been the subject of many investigations recently. At these scales, flows are generally laminar and governed mainly by viscous and interfacial forces, while inertial and gravity forces are small. The thin [fluidic](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/fluidics "Learn more about fluidic from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") films and small fluid volumes improve heat and mass transfer rates which result in more uniform concentration and [temperature fields](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical-engineering/temperature- distribution "Learn more about temperature fields from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") and allow better process control compared to [large scale systems](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/large-scale- systems "Learn more about large scale systems from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages"); these features can enhance efficiency and reduce waste [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177715001995#b0025). [Microchannel](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microchannel "Learn more about Microchannel from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [multiphase flows](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/multiphase-flows "Learn more about multiphase flows from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") in particular have found many applications in areas such as chemical analysis and synthesis, pharmaceuticals processing and thermal management systems [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177715001995#b0015), [[30]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177715001995#b0150). The increased surface to volume ratio in microchannels favours multiphase processes where interfacial mass or heat transfer are important.

[Microfluidic](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidics "Learn more about Microfluidic from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") tools play an important role in generating and handling nanoliter/microliter fluid droplets or bubbles [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000015). Microfluidic methods for forming droplets can be either active or positive. Most methods are passive, relying on the flow field to deform the interface and promote the natural growth of interfacial instabilities [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000025), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000030), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000035). Passive microfluidic methods can be listed into three categories, characterized by the nature of the flow field near pinch-off: (1) droplet breakup in co-flowing streams [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000040), [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000045), (2) droplet breakup in cross-flowing stream [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000050), [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000055), and (3) breakup in elongational or stretching dominated flows [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000025), [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000060). One of the central goals of studying the flow of droplets in microfluidic channels is to understand the mechanisms which govern the partitioning of droplets at the nodes. When a droplet reaches a symmetric or asymmetric bifurcation, it flows into the branch having larger [volumetric](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/volumetrics "Learn more about volumetric from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") flow rate [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000065), [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000070), [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000075). The nonuniform partitioning of droplets is a common phenomenon in the process of blood plasma separation. Continuous blood plasma separation which is sometimes called Zweifach–Fung effect [[16]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000080), [[17]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000085) is demonstrated experimentally using simple [microfluidic devices](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidic-device "Learn more about microfluidic devices from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [[18]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000090), [[19]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000095), [[20]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000100), [[21]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000105), [[22]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000110), [[23]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000115), [[24]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000120), [[25]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000125), [[26]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0997754615300765#br000130).

Micro/millimeter-scale reactors provide efficient mass and heat transfer with the internal circulation flow, which is quite suitable for various syntheses [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894719329055#b0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894719329055#b0010). These reactors with T-junctions, in particular, have attracted much attention for gas-liquid reactions. They have recently been used, for instance, to achieve technological advances in the area of organic synthesis [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894719329055#b0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894719329055#b0020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894719329055#b0025). In gas-liquid slug flow, rapid mixing and mass transfer between two phases can simultaneously be achieved via the internal circulation flow. These features enable one to obtain high yields of gas-liquid reactions at specific temperatures and pressures than those of the conventional systems [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894719329055#b0030), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894719329055#b0035).

In the recent years, a growing interest in the study of gas–liquid flows has arisen as a consequence of their promising technological applications in space [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0045793011003586#b0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0045793011003586#b0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0045793011003586#b0015). Replacing the widely used single-phase for two-phase systems could lead to an improvement in performance as well as to significant reductions in weight in different fields such as power generation and life support. A good understanding of the behavior of the gas–liquid interfaces is the cornerstone of these new technologies.

The droplet formation from a two-liquid system in a [microfluidic device](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidic-device "Learn more about microfluidic device from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") is a fundamental process in [multiphase flow](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/multiphase-flows "Learn more about multiphase flow from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"). The phenomenon has been extensively investigated during the last few decades due to its applications in numerous fields such as biotechnology, pharmaceutical, and chemical industries ([Avesar et al., 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222001823#bib0004); [Casadevall et al., 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222001823#bib0012); [Song et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222001823#bib0047); [Song et al., 2003](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222001823#bib0048); [Teh et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222001823#bib0050)). Understanding droplet formation, their stabilities, and the two-phase flow characteristics are essential for designing various [microfluidic](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidics "Learn more about microfluidic from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") devices. Micro-sized droplets having a high surface-to-volume ratio enable rapid reaction in two-phase fluid systems, and the process is helpful for several diagnostic applications ([Yao et al., 2018](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222001823#bib0056)). Moreover, [microscale](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microscale "Learn more about microscale from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") flow patterns and the extended surface area due to droplet formation essentially facilitate the heat and mass transfer, which are pre-requisites for the optimum design of several micro-structured devices ([Seemann et al., 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222001823#bib0046); [Teh et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301932222001823#bib0050)).

[Thorsen et al. (2001)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib16) were the first to show [emulsification](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/emulsification "Learn more about emulsification from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") at T-junctions in 2001. Ever since, the use of T-junctions has been reported for the preparation of, e.g. [double emulsions](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical-engineering/multiple- emulsion "Learn more about double emulsions from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") ([Barbier et al., 2006a](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib1); [Nisisako et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib11); [Okushima et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib13)) and microspheres ([Nisisako and Torii, 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib12); [Nisisako et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib10)), as well as in (bio)chemical analysis ([Tice et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib17); [Zheng and Ismagilov, 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib20)). Droplets prepared at T-junctions are typically between several up to hundreds of micrometres in size ([Garstecki et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib4); [Graaf et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib6), [Graaf et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib7); [Nisisako et al., 2002](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib9), [Nisisako et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib10); [Zhao et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib18); see [Table 1](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#tbl1)) and have a polydispersity index (standard deviation to average droplet size ratio) below 5% ([Nisisako and Torii, 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib12)), which implies acceptable [monodispersity](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/monodispersity "Learn more about monodispersity from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"). Per T-junction, up to several thousands of droplets can be produced per second ([Nisisako et al., 2002](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib9)). Though this production rate is quite adequate, the accompanying volume throughput is too low to meet demands for industrial-scale emulsification ([Nisisako and Torii, 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib12)). Therefore, T-junctions have been parallelised ([Barbier et al., 2006b](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib2); [Nisisako and Torii, 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib12); [Zheng et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib19)). [Nisisako and Torii (2008)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S000925090900181X#bib12) were the first to operate 256 T-junctions simultaneously and showed that neither droplet size nor monodispersity is influenced by parallelisation, which is an important step towards actual application.

The spreading dynamics of a droplet on a solid surface has been studied for more than two centuries [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0025). Applications of this phenomenon can be seen from fuel injection, spray painting, surface cooling, coatings on surfaces, adhesion, and [inkjet printing](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/inkjet-printing "Learn more about inkjet printing from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") to some common natural phenomenon such as oil spreading on fish scales, raindrops falling on leaves, and more [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0025), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0030), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0035), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0040). Drops of different sizes, speeds and materials have an impact on the surfaces which defines the effectiveness and efficiency of a particular operation. For example, heat transfer in spray cooling process of a steel slab depends on the amount and speed of the [liquid droplets](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/liquid-droplet "Learn more about liquid droplets from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") spreading on a solid surface. For this reason, the entire spreading procedure, from start to finish, is very important to understand. Several factors have an impact on the spreading of a droplet. To have a better understanding on the role of these factors, it is important to segregate each parameter of interest and study its effect. The effect of one such factor is pressure surrounding the droplet. In order to estimate the effects of pressure on wetting dynamics, several studies have been carried out in relation to oil recovery systems to evaluate the geo-storage of CO2 in porous aquifers. A number of studies [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0045), [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0050), [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0055) have been conducted to investigate the effects of surrounding pressure on the wettability and surface [free energy](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical-engineering/gibbs-free- energy "Learn more about free energy from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") of [surface coatings](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/surface-coating "Learn more about surface coatings from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"). The wettability of water was found to be poor on [Polytetrafluoroethylene](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/polytetrafluoroethylene "Learn more about Polytetrafluoroethylene from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") (PTFE), intermediate on stainless steel and good for [glass substrates](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/glass-substrate "Learn more about glass substrates from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") in a pressure range of 0.1–27 MPa and 40℃ [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0055). However, these studies do not consider pressure effects on the initial spreading and the associated transition to later regimes. Initial spreading dictates the final contour of the drop as well as the [equilibrium contact angle](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/equilibrium-contact- angle "Learn more about equilibrium contact angle from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages"). In this paper, we investigate experientially the early time spreading dynamics on a solid substrate while considering a change in surrounding pressure, the results from which can be used to improve high pressure [engineering processes](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/process- engineering "Learn more about engineering processes from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") such as refining, extraction, refrigeration, polymer foaming, polymerisation, pressing of oil seeds, etc [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0894177721000996#b0055).

In the last decade, the interest in the interactions between two immiscible fluids (liquid/liquid or liquid/gas) by converging a dispersed phase (break-up stream) and a continuous phase (shear stream) has risen significantly. Indeed, several microsystems were developed and many studies have been carried out and extended to multiphase flow, in order to improve the industrial microfluidic devices employing calibrated bubbles and droplets. In this respect, some of the main investigations have been reviewed lately ([Baroud et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib3), [Zhao and Middelberg, 2011](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib32)) focusing on the physical mechanisms governing the bubble production in various microfluidic devices. Furthermore, three fundamental techniques have been widely employed to product droplets and bubbles: (i) the co-flowing streams ([Kreutzer et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib18), [Guillot et al., 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib15), [Utada et al., 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib24), [Utada et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib25)), (ii) the cross-flowing streams ([Thorsen et al., 2001](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib23), [Garstecki et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib14), [de Menech et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib7), [Xu et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib30), [Fu et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib13), [van Steijn et al., 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib26), [van Steijn et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib27)) and (iii) the microfluidic flow focusing devices ([Anna et al., 2003](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib2), [Dreyfus et al., 2003](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib12), [Xu et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib29), [Takeuchi et al., 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250912004964#bib21)). As for flows with low Reynolds numbers, the use of microchannels in the above- named systems allows to consider only the viscous and interfacial effects when describing the dynamic formation of calibrated bubbles and droplets.

Droplet formation of one fluid in a second immiscible fluid is useful in a wide range of applications, such as cell encapsulation [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0005), drug delivery [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0010), biochemistry analysis [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0015) and so on, where micro-fluidic techniques have drawn growing interest in recent years for highly controlled formation of droplets [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0025), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0030), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0035), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0040). Various micro-fluidic devices have been advanced to generate mono-dispersed droplets, including T-shaped channel [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0035), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0040), [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0045), flow-focusing method [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0050), [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0055), [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0060), [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0065), micro-channel array [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0070), neck-cavity geometry [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0075), collision-shearing mode [[16]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894711009867#bib0080), etc. Among these the T-junction geometry is one of the most frequently used devices.

As a result of demand and development of [microfabrication](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/microfabrication "Learn more about microfabrication from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), pharmaceutical industry, biochemical application, etc., there is a growing interest in bubbles or droplets formation and precise control (for monosized emulsion) using microfluidic devices ([Stone et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911007627#bib35), [Squires and Quake, 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250911007627#bib32)), with particularly designed layouts of microchannels, as comprehensively reviewed by [Tan et al. Being aware of the potential in microfluidic technology, the bubble-based microfluidics have been introduced as an attractive option to produce and manipulate bubbles for various applications, including chemical reaction and mixing process, bio-chemical and logic microfluidic system, medical diagnostic and treatments, etc. [1.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2095927316301256#bib1), [2.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2095927316301256#bib2), [3.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2095927316301256#bib3), [4.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2095927316301256#bib4), [5.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2095927316301256#bib5), [6.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2095927316301256#bib6). As one of the basic “unit operation element” of bubble-based microfluidics, T-junction is frequently encountered in these applications for the bubble generation and breakup as well as the mass transfer and mixing enhancement. The absence of nonlinear bubble dynamics and the evolution of complicated interface topologies are involved during the bubble breakup process. In particular, the bubble breakup process in a T-shaped [microchannel](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary- sciences/microchannel "Learn more about microchannel from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") is coupled with the bubble motion, deformation and [coalescence](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/coalescence "Learn more about coalescence from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), which complicates the precise control of bubble size via T-junction microfluidic [7.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2095927316301256#bib7), [8.](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2095927316301256#bib8). Therefore, it is of great significance to fully understand the breakup behaviors of bubbles in a microfluidic T-junction, so as to provide theoretical support for the accurate manipulation of bubble.

The transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) materials, due to two dimensional (2D) nature, have unique electrical, optical, chemical, and [mechanical properties](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials-science/mechanical- property "Learn more about mechanical properties from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages"), making them highly attractive for device applications [[[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib1), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib2), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib3), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib4), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib5)]. Dimensionally and strain controlled [electronic band structure](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials-science/electronic- band-structure "Learn more about electronic band structure from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") in these materials provide an opportunity to engineer the properties in functional devices [[6](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib6)]. Reduced dimensionality of these materials could be utilized to realize sub-10-nm node devices for practical applications [[7](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib7)]. Integrated circuits, switches, amplifiers have been realized in monolayer MoS2 based electronic devices [[[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib8), [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib9), [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib10)]. Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) based microprocessor having 115 transistors was fabricated for 1-bit data processing capability [[11](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib11)]. Even [superconductivity](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/superconductivity "Learn more about superconductivity from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") was observed in the 20 nm thick MoS2 layer gated with the [ionic liquid](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials-science/ionic-liquid "Learn more about ionic liquid from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [[12](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib12)]. Among 2D TMDs, MoS2 has attained considerable attention as a functional material due to its easily tunable electronic properties [[[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib13), [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib14), [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib15)]. MoS2 has a layered structure with interlayer weak van der Waals attraction. Multi-layers (unit cells) of MoS2 has an indirect band gap of 1.2 eV, which changes to direct band gap (1.9 eV) for a monolayer of MoS2 [[16](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib16),[17](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib17)]. The layer dependent transition of the indirect to direct band gap can be observed in the enhanced [photoluminescence](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/photoluminescence "Learn more about photoluminescence from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") of single-layer MoS2 which can be utilized in functional [optoelectronic](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/optoelectronics "Learn more about optoelectronic from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") devices [[18](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib18)], presence of bandgap in single layer MoS2 leads to the fabrication of [field effect transistors](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/field-effect-transistors "Learn more about field effect transistors from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") with room temperature current on-off ratio of 108. Although the electronic mobility of single-layer MoS2 and other TMD semiconductors is rather low in comparison to graphene [[8](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib8),[19](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib19)]. The presence of a [dielectric](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/dielectric-material "Learn more about dielectric from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") like HfO2 in the proximity of single-layer MoS2 enhances the electronic mobility significantly at room temperature [[8](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib8),[18](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib18),[20](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092583881931686X#bib20)]. Fluid flow is one of the most fundamental phenomena in nature, and in recent years, [microfluidics](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/physics-and- astronomy/microfluidics "Learn more about microfluidics from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") has shown a strong development trend with the booming development of Micro-Electro-Mechanical System(MEMS). Microfluidics is a science and technology for manipulating fluids on the micron scale. The functions of biological and chemical laboratories can be performed on a chip of a few square centimeters [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0001), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0002). Microdroplet technology is an important branch of microfluidics. Microdroplets are generated due to fluid instability, but it is difficult to prepare droplets of a few microns in size. There are two kinds of droplet generation methods, one is the active method and the other is the passive method. The passive method is the most common and simplest method, and the commonly used passive methods are T-junction channel method, flow-focusing method, co-flow focusing method [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0003), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0004). The T-junction microchannel method is the simplest and most commonly used method.Thorsen et al. first proposed the T-junction microchannel method to generate droplets and pointed out that shear force and interfacial tension are important factors causing droplet fragmentation [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0005). Han et al. investigated the mechanism of microdroplet generation in T-junction microchannel by numerical simulation and discussed the effects of flow rate ratio, continuous phase viscosity, contact angle, interfacial tension and other factors on droplet size. And a T-junction microchannel with a step was designed to solve the problem of pressure in the channel [[6](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0006),[7](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0007)]. Xu et al. investigated the mechanism of droplet formation at different capillary numbers and predicted the droplet size by varying the capillary number [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0008). Anna et al. designed a flow focusing apparatus to prepare droplets from two immiscible liquids and concluded that the size of the droplets depends to a large extent on the flow rate [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0009). Han et al. investigated the mechanism of droplet generation in a flow focusing device by numerical simulation and discussed the effects of interfacial tension, flow rate ratio, contact angle, continuous phase viscosity, channel shape and channel width-to-height ratio on droplet size [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0010), [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0011), [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0012). Wu et al. experimentally explained the stable dripping-bifurcation-dripping in flow-focusing devices and found that this phenomenon, obtained at low flow conditions, strongly depends on the length of the orifice plate, implying that inertia and capillary pressure control this state [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0013). A co-flow focusing device for the preparation of emulsified droplets was developed by Umbanhowar et al. This device has the advantages of droplet stability and few satellite droplets. Since the generated droplets are not limited by the shape of the channel, the droplet size can be precisely controlled by varying the flow rate of the continuous phase [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0014). Numerical simulations of the generation of non-Newtonian droplets in a Co-flow focusing device were performed by Taassob et al. The results of the study showed that the flow rate of the continuous phase has a more significant effect on the droplets in the jetting state, and the droplet volume is less dependent on the viscosity of the dispersed phase [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0015). The effects of ratio of density, ratio of viscosity, capillary number and Weber number on droplet volume were investigated by Shahin et al. [[16]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0016). The effects of wall effects, ratio of flow rates, interfacial tension and viscosity of the continuous phase on droplet size were investigated experimentally and numerically by Deng et al. [[17]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0017). Rahimi et al. investigated the effect of local geometry on droplet formation in a coaxial focusing device, including the diameter of the dispersed phase channel, the depth of the nozzle into the channel, and the inner diameter and length of the continuous phase channel [[18]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0018). Xu et al. developed a device for measuring the differential pressure of capillary devices that clearly identifies the transition between dripping and jetting [[19]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0960077921011280#bib0019)

Nucleation is considered the most critical step in crystallization processes, because it impacts several crystal properties, including [crystal size distribution](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/crystal-size- distribution "Learn more about crystal size distribution from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") and polymorphism. Both of these characteristics are very important for downstream processes and decisive in drug development. Nucleation is known to have a stochastic nature ([Kulkarni et al., 2013](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876218304441#bib0065), [Goh et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876218304441#bib0035), [Kubota, 2015](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876218304441#bib0060)). This characteristic poses challenges to obtaining reproducible experimental data, and therefore numerous identical experiments are essential to correctly build probability distributions for studying the [stochastic behaviour](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/stochastic- behavior "Learn more about stochastic behaviour from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") of [primary nucleation](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/primary- nucleation "Learn more about primary nucleation from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages"). Crystal detection times, as well as nucleation times, _t_ _N_ , are volume dependent; in particular _t_ _N_ ∝ 1/ _JV_ , where _J_ is the [nucleation rate](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/nucleation-rate "Learn more about nucleation rate from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") and _V_ is the volume of the [crystallizer](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/crystallizer "Learn more about crystallizer from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") ([Kubota, 2015](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876218304441#bib0060)). Besides carrying out numerous experiments, reproducibility of volumes is also fundamental to avoid introducing further variability in the probability distributions associated with the repeated nucleation measurements. If this is achieved, robust statistics can be obtained and [nucleation mechanism](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/nucleation- mechanism "Learn more about nucleation mechanism from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") and kinetics can reliably be determined.

Horn antennas are those of most common types of antennas in the field of [satellite communication](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/computer- science/satellite-communication-network "Learn more about satellite communication from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), defense industry and radars due to high [directivity](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/directivity "Learn more about directivity from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") and wide bandwidth, its simplicity, ease of production and high efficiency [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1434841117330273#b0005), and horn arrays commonly finds usage in satellite communications and [radar systems](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/radar-systems "Learn more about radar systems from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") due to their increased gain [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1434841117330273#b0010). They are also used as a standard measurement reference element for calibrations and as a feeding element for dish [reflector antennas](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/reflector-antennas "Learn more about reflector antennas from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") in satellite systems. Radiation characteristic of a pyramid horn antenna is a combination of E-plane and H-plane sectorial horn antennas, and they have linearly polarized radiation [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1434841117330273#b0015).

Microfluidic devices are distinguished by microchannels with widths in the order of 100 μm involving two or more different fluids with typical flow rates of a few μL/s. They are found in various configurations such as T-junction, co-axial flow, and focused-flow ([Baroud et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915006478#bib1)). The low Reynolds number (Re) and high [Peclet number](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical-engineering/peclet- number "Learn more about Peclet number from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") (Pe) nature of these devices facilitates the formation of highly- controlled monodispersed microdroplets for efficient chemical transport ([Squires and Quake, 2005](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915006478#bib23), [Stone et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250915006478#bib24)). _Nesopora caninum_ , a protozoan pathogen which causes reproductive failure in cattle, has acquired an intracellular lifecycle by means of sequential events in its lytic cycle that result in intracellular proliferation and dissemination of tachyzoites into the host. The lytic cycle has been carefully studied in the closely related parasite _T. gondii_. However, due to the high similarity displayed by both parasites (e.g. secretory organelles, orthologue proteins, and _in vitro_ replication), it is believed that most described mechanisms for _T. gondii_ could also apply for _N. caninum_. During the lytic cycle, the parasite reaches the host cell by gliding motility and re- orientates itself towards the cell surface. Initial host cell recognition, adhesion and invasion are mediated by parasite surface antigens [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S187439191100042X#bb0005) and the orchestrated secretion of a protein arsenal [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S187439191100042X#bb0010) from the specialised microneme and rhoptry of the parasite apical complex, together with dense granule secretory organelles. Proteins from these organelles are also implicated in the formation and modelling of the parasitophorous vacuole (PV) inside the host cell and in stimulating host immune responses. Thus, identifying and characterizing components of the secretory organelles will lead to a better comprehension of the invasion process and may also identify vaccine candidates [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S187439191100042X#bb0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S187439191100042X#bb0020).

Naturally derived polysaccharides such as chitosan, alginate and hyaluronic acid are widely used in biomedical engineering. Extensive attention has been focused on utilizing such natural materials in drug, enzyme or protein delivery ([Jameela et al., 1994](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0144861709005797#bib3), [Wang et al., 2007](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0144861709005797#bib14)), wound dressings, as well as scaffolds for tissue engineering ([Mjahed, Porcel, Senger, et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0144861709005797#bib6)). Whether in the form of microspheres, multilayer films or scaffolds, their polyelectrolytic and hydrophilic properties make them excellent protective matrices for small bioactive molecules such as BSA, insulin or other growth factors as well as cells ([Zhang, Cai, Bei, & Wang, 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0144861709005797#bib16)). Therefore, controlled processing of these polymeric materials is of great importance, aiming at fabrication of specifically designed surfaces and interior structures. Many conventional processing techniques, involving the use of organic solvents or harsh conditions, are not suitable to process natural polymers, because the product cannot preserve the inherent cell- affinity of these polymers.
