In recent years, [microfluidic](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidics "Learn more about microfluidic from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") chips have been widely used in scientific research fields such as biochemistry ([Mashaghi et al., 2016](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219301017#bib0100)) and microsystem engineering ([Chen et al., 2013,](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219301017#bib0030) [2016a,](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219301017#bib0035) [2016b](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219301017#bib0040); [Chen and Li, 2016,](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219301017#bib0020) [2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219301017#bib0025); [Chen and Zhang, 2018](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219301017#bib0055); [Chen and Zhao, 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219301017#bib0060); [Chen et al., 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219301017#bib0050)). The use of droplet-based microfluidics is particularly prominent. Droplet [microfluidic technology](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidic- technology "Learn more about microfluidic technology from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") is a promising interdisciplinary technology for the production and manipulation of monodisperse micro/nano droplets ([Shang et al., 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219301017#bib0140)). Droplet microfluidic technology has many incomparable advantages over traditional fluid control technology ([Baroud et al., 2010](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219301017#bib0010)). The high surface area to volume ratio of the droplets accelerates the chemical microreaction and increases the rate of reaction ([Dubois et al., 2006](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219301017#bib0075)). The volume of the droplet is mostly nanoliter, thus greatly reducing the consumption of samples and reagents. Droplet microfluidic technology is now widely used in new materials synthesis ([Ran et al., 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219301017#bib0125)), chemical and biological analysis ([Chiu et al., 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219301017#bib0065)) organ chips ([Bhatia and Ingber, 2014](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0263876219301017#bib0015)).

As droplet microfluidics have been widely applied in medical, biological and chemical research ([Hou et al., 2017](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921007715#b0060), [Hale et al., 2018](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921007715#b0055), [Rane et al., 2012](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921007715#b0110)), how to precisely control the size of the droplets is of great importance for the applications of droplet microfluidic systems ([Zhang et al., 2020](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921007715#b0165), [Li et al., 2019](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921007715#b0080), [Schuler et al., 2016](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921007715#b0115)), such as particle synthesis and digital polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Especially compared with the conventional real-time PCR ([Zhang et al., 2019](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921007715#b0160)); the droplet digital PCR has great advantages of high detection sensitivity, high detection accuracy and high integration ([Zhang and Jiang, 2016](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921007715#b0155)). In addition, the droplet digital PCR can overcome the disadvantages of the conventional real-time PCR, such as sample contamination, sample loss, low detection sensitivity and complicated operating process ([Pan et al., 2020](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921007715#b0100)). More importantly, the detection accuracy of nucleic acid can be increased significantly by precisely controlling the size of the droplets formed in the microfluidic device for the droplet digital PCR ([Zhuang et al., 2020](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250921007715#b0170)).

Monodispersed small bubbles and droplets are important spaces and mediums for ultrasound imaging [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0005), targeted drug delivery [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0010), single-cell sequencing [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0015), chemical reactions and material preparations [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0025), [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0030), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0035), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0040). Compared with conventional bubble and droplet generation methods, microfluidic chip shows its significant advantages for producing monodispersed (CV < 5%) bubbles and droplets in recent years [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0045), [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0050), [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0055), [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0060), [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0065). Researchers have realized monodispersed bubble and droplet generation within micro-devices with different means for wide applications [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0070), [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0075), [[16]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0080), [[17]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0085), [[18]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0090), [[19]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1385894716301759#b0095). However, generating monodispersed small bubbles and droplets (<50 μm) remains technically challenging, for small bubbles and droplets often come with small channels, which always demands for tedious fabrication and costly materials.

[Microfluidics](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidics "Learn more about Microfluidics from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") can handle or manipulate the fluid in the [microchannels](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microchannel "Learn more about microchannels from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") ranging in size from tens to hundreds of micrometers [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0016003220301307#bib0001). Since the early 1980s, it has become an emerging interdiscipline involving chemical, [fluid physics](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/fluid-physic "Learn more about fluid physics from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), microelectronics, materials science, biology and [biomedical engineering](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/biomedical- engineering "Learn more about biomedical engineering from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages"), which has the characteristics of miniaturization, integration, etc. [Microfluidic devices](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microfluidic-device "Learn more about Microfluidic devices from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") are commonly referred to as microfluidic chips, also known as Lab on a Chip. Microfluidic droplet technique [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0016003220301307#bib0002) is a new technology developed on the basis of microfluidics to study the formation, manipulation and application of microdroplets of a few micrometers size. The T-junction structure is one of the most versatile microchannel structures used to generate droplets in microfluidic devices [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0016003220301307#bib0003). During the formation of microdroplets, two incompressible and incompatible [Newtonian fluids](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/newtonian- fluid "Learn more about Newtonian fluids from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") are selected as continuous phase and [dispersed phase](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/dispersed-phase "Learn more about dispersed phase from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), which are injected into the two entrances of the microchannel respectively [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0016003220301307#bib0004). When the two fluids meet at the T-junction, the dispersed phase forms a _plug_ shape because of the shear and extrusion of the continuous phase fluid, and ruptures due to the instability of interfacial tension. Finally, the microdroplets form and disperse in the continuous phase. Microdroplets, often used as [microreactor](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/microreactor "Learn more about microreactor from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), realizes [biochemical](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/biochemicals "Learn more about biochemical from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") reaction, rapid reagent mixing and microparticle synthesis etc. It drastically enhances the advantages of microfluidics in terms of low consumption, automation and [high throughput](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/computer-science/high- throughput "Learn more about high throughput from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") and is widely used in drug delivery [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0016003220301307#bib0005), chemical synthesis [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0016003220301307#bib0006), microextraction [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0016003220301307#bib0007), enzyme synthesis [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0016003220301307#bib0008), [cell encapsulation](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/cell- encapsulation "Learn more about cell encapsulation from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0016003220301307#bib0009), and many other fields.

Droplets have been widely developed in recent years because they have a variety of applications, such as urea detection, reaction containers, crystallizing proteins and sorting cells, etc [[1](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092540051930869X#bib0005),[2](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092540051930869X#bib0010)]. The fluid pairs to form the droplets include gas and water [[3](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092540051930869X#bib0015)], water and water [[4](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092540051930869X#bib0020)], gas and oil [[5](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092540051930869X#bib0025)], oil and water [[6](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092540051930869X#bib0030)] and oil and oil [[7](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092540051930869X#bib0035)]. In the aqueous systems (gas-water, water-water, and oil-water), aqueous residues can promote a premature payload release [[8](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092540051930869X#bib0040)]. Also, many systems react with water and generate undesired by-products [[9](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092540051930869X#bib0045)]. In some systems, for example, engines in some [mechanical systems](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/mechanical-systems "Learn more about mechanical systems from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), it is usually easy for rust to form when cleaner is combined with water; the sol-gel process with metal alkoxides should be done implemented without water [[10](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092540051930869X#bib0050)]. Therefore, an entirely water-free system is urgently required for these systems. As a promising approach, the O/O (oil-in-oil) droplet system can produce droplets in a non-aqueous environment. The O/O droplets are attractive for a large number of fields of research, e.g., pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, personal care, and electronics. The oil pairs include nonpolar solvents such as hydrocarbons and highly [polar solvents](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/polar-solvent "Learn more about polar solvents from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") like [formamide](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/formamide "Learn more about formamide from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"). In the last ten decades, various types of oil pairs have been reported [[11](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092540051930869X#bib0055)]: [polyamine](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/polyamine "Learn more about polyamine from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") / hydrocarbon oil; [triglyceride](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/triglyceride "Learn more about triglyceride from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") oil / [silicone oil](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/silicone-oil "Learn more about silicone oil from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"); silicone oil / [thermotropic liquid crystal](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/thermotropic-liquid- crystal "Learn more about thermotropic liquid crystal from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages"); [castor oil](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/castor-oil "Learn more about castor oil from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") / silicone oil; silicone oil / fluorinated oil; silicone oil / chlorinated paraffin oil; silicone oil / vegetable oil; and so on. The [emulsifiers](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/emulsifier "Learn more about emulsifiers from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") used to stabilize the droplets can be primarily divided into the surfactants [[12](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092540051930869X#bib0060)], Pickering particles [[13](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092540051930869X#bib0065)] and [block polymer](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/block- copolymer "Learn more about block polymer from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [[14](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S092540051930869X#bib0070)]. Our paper considers the mixture of immiscible oils stabilized by surfactants, which is the conventional method to stabilize the droplets.

In the last two decades, microreactors have emerged as promising devices to produce chemicals due to their large surface-to-volume ratio, enhanced mass transfer rate, and safety ([Reyes et al., 2002](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250922004584#b0125), [Vilkner et al., 2004](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250922004584#b0190)). Small volume droplets generated in microreactors are indispensable in many applications, such as bio-chemical and material synthesis, drug discovery, medical diagnostics and treatments ([Teh et al., 2008](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0009250922004584#b0175)). To design microfluidic devices for above mentioned applications, it is essential to accurately predict the flow pattern and droplet size, which are determined by the fluid properties, flow rate ratio of the dispersed phase to the continuous phase, and the configuration of the microfluidic devices.

Microfluidic platforms provide an excellent capability in controlling fluid flow, heat and mass transport for [chemical engineering](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/chemical-engineering "Learn more about chemical engineering from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), pharmaceutical industry, material science and biochemical application [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0005), [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0020), [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0025). There is a growing interest in precise controlling bubbles or droplets formation _via_ microfluidic devices [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0030), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0035), where the liquid phase physical properties such as viscosity and surface tension profoundly affects fluid flow behavior [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0040). Recently, Taylor flow has received extensive attentions for wide operating range, little liquid back-mixing and high mono-dispersity [[9]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0045), [[10]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0050). Bubbles are always encountered in Taylor flow in microchannel and manipulation of the bubble size is of great importance for microanalysis, on-chip separation, and micro-chemical reaction [[11]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0055). T-junction is the most employed inlet geometry to produce bubble/droplet and passively tailor the bubble/droplet size. Therefore, the regulation and predication of the Taylor bubble/slug length in T-junction microchannel are crucial issue for the application of the microfluidic technique. The bubble breakup and formation process involve complex mechanism in microchannel, which is mainly relevant to drag force competition from interfacial tension, viscous shearing and possible force perturbations out of the system. These forces originate from three aspects [[12]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0060), [[13]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0065): properties of the fluids (viscosity and surface tension), configuration of the microchannel (cross-section geometry and gas/liquid inlet contact angle) and fluid flow conditions (gas/liquid flow rate or velocity). Numerous works, either the process of breakup or quantitative analysis of the bubble/droplet size, have been conducted recently [[14]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0070), [[15]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0075), [[16]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0080), [[17]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0085), [[18]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0090), [[19]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0095), [[20]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0100), [[21]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0105), [[22]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0110), [[23]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0115), [[24]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0120), [[25]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0125), [[26]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0130), [[27]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1004954118315593#bb0135).

Droplet based [microfluidics](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/microfluidics "Learn more about microfluidics from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") as characterised by droplet splitting, merging, squeezing, slipping has been emerging as one of the most sound and prominent research topic owing to its applications in inkjet printing [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775721017428#bib1), droplet mixing [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775721017428#bib2), cooling system [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775721017428#bib3), [double emulsions](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/multiple-emulsion "Learn more about double emulsions from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775721017428#bib4), drug transport [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0927775721017428#bib5), to name a few. This has triggered demand for the generation of droplet in a verse domain and great adoration of research on various droplet based transport processes within microchannels. In this context, droplet splitting is an important operation in droplet-based microfluidics which is used to exercise control over droplet volume after production and thus enhancing the operational flexibility. Further, it may be noted that droplet splitting where, a single droplet pinches off into two or more smaller droplets is influenced by geometric configuration of the channel, surface properties of the channels like [wettability](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/wettability "Learn more about wettability from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages") along with flow conditions [like capillary](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemistry/capillary-crystal "Learn more about like capillary from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages") number, and viscous forces. Moreover, these decisive factors can yield to different flow regimes like splitting and non-splitting regime, which is quiet fascinating to explore in further details for the research community for the sake of precise realization of the encountered flow dynamics, both from fundamental as well as applied perspective and hence, requires in-depth investigation.

The liquid-liquid mass transfer processes serve as the foundation for numerous chemical reactions, such as [nitration](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/nitration "Learn more about nitration from ScienceDirect's AI- generated Topic Pages"), [emulsion polymerization](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/materials- science/emulsion-polymerization "Learn more about emulsion polymerization from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), diazonium reactions, and separation processes like extraction and precipitation [[1]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1383586623013485#b0005). Therefore, it is of great significance to study the mass transfer law in liquid-liquid systems. With an improved understanding of mass transfer processes, the intensification of mass transfer has gradually become a popular research area. Various types of reactors, including stirred tank reactor, [membrane reactor](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/chemical- engineering/membrane-reactor "Learn more about membrane reactor from ScienceDirect's AI-generated Topic Pages"), and rotary reactor, have been developed to enhance mass transfer [[2]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1383586623013485#b0010), [[3]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1383586623013485#b0015), [[4]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1383586623013485#b0020). However, for many fast liquid-liquid reactions, conventional reactors fail to provide the required mass transfer performance to meet the demands of reaction kinetics [[5]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1383586623013485#b0025). Inadequate mass transfer performance often becomes the rate-determining step in the fast reaction processes, limiting reaction efficiency and potentially leading to side reactions [[6]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1383586623013485#b0030), [[7]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1383586623013485#b0035), [[8]](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1383586623013485#b0040). Therefore, the development of novel reactors that can provide much higher mass transfer performance is of utmost importance.
